title.zh: 卷一百五十七 列傳第四十四: 劉秉忠 張文謙 郝經
title.en: Volume 157 Biographies 44: Liu Bingzhong, Zhang Wenqian, Hao Jing
title.raw: 卷一百五十七 列傳第四十四: 劉秉忠 張文謙 郝經 Volume 157 Biographies 44: Liu Bingzhong, Zhang Wenqian, Hao Jing

sentences.zh: 劉秉忠

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong

sentences.zh: 劉秉忠，字仲晦，初名侃，因從釋氏，又名子聰，拜官後始更今名。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhong, style name Zhonghui; his original name was Kan; because he followed the Buddhist order he was also called Zicong; he adopted his present name only after receiving official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong, styled Zhonghui, was originally named Kan. Having entered the Buddhist clergy he was also known as Zicong, and took his present name only after he received office.

sentences.zh: 其先瑞州人也，世仕遼，為官族。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Ruizhou; for generations they served the Liao and were an official clan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were from Ruizhou; for generations they served the Liao dynasty and formed a family of officials.

sentences.zh: 曾大父仕金，為邢州節度副使，因家焉，故自大父澤而下，遂為邢人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather served the Jin as deputy military commissioner of Xingzhou and settled his family there; thus from his grandfather Ze downward they became men of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather served the Jin as deputy military commissioner of Xingzhou and established the family there, so from his grandfather Ze onward they were counted as men of Xing.

sentences.zh: 庚辰歲，木華黎取邢州，立都元帥府，以其父潤為都統。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year Muqali took Xingzhou, established the supreme command headquarters, and appointed his father Run as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year Muqali captured Xingzhou, set up a supreme command headquarters, and appointed his father Run as its commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 事定，改署州錄事，歷鉅鹿、內丘兩縣提領，所至皆有惠愛。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Run was reassigned as recorder of the prefecture; he served in succession as chief administrator of Julu and Neiqiu counties, and wherever he went he showed kindness and care.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored he was reassigned as prefectural recorder, then served in turn as chief administrator of Julu and Neiqiu counties; everywhere he went he won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 秉忠生而風骨秀異，志氣英爽不羈。

translations.literal: Bingzhong was born with outstanding bearing and an unconstrained, spirited temperament.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong was born with striking presence and a bold, unfettered spirit.

sentences.zh: 八歲入學，日誦數百言。

translations.literal: At eight he entered school and could recite several hundred words a day.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he began his studies and could recite several hundred characters each day.

sentences.zh: 年十三，為質子於帥府。

translations.literal: At thirteen he became a hostage at the command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he was sent as a hostage to the command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十七，為邢台節度使府令史，以養其親。

translations.literal: At seventeen he became a clerk in the Xingtai military commissioner's office to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he became a clerk in the Xingtai military commissioner's office in order to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 居常鬱鬱不樂，一日，投筆歎曰：「吾家累世衣冠，乃汨沒為刀筆吏乎！

translations.literal: He was often depressed and unhappy; one day he threw down his brush and sighed: "For generations my family has worn caps and robes—am I to sink into being a mere clerk with knife and brush?
translations.idiomatic: He was often gloomy and discontented. One day he cast aside his brush and sighed: "For generations my family has been gentry—must I sink to life as a petty clerk with knife and brush?

sentences.zh: 丈夫不遇於世，當隱居以求志耳。」

translations.literal: When a man meets no recognition in the world, he ought to withdraw and seek his purpose in seclusion."
translations.idiomatic: When a man finds no place in the world, he should withdraw and pursue his purpose in seclusion."

sentences.zh: 即棄去，​​隱武安山中。

translations.literal: With that he left his post and withdrew to seclusion in the Wuan mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At once he resigned and went into seclusion in the Wuan mountains.

sentences.zh: 久之，天寧虛照禪師遣徒招致為僧，以其能文詞，使掌書記。

translations.literal: After some time Chan Master Xuzhao of Tianning sent disciples to invite him and ordain him as a monk; because of his literary skill he was made to manage correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: After a time Chan Master Xuzhao of Tianning sent disciples to fetch him and have him ordained; because he excelled at literary composition he was put in charge of correspondence.

sentences.zh: 後遊雲中，留居南堂寺。

translations.literal: Later he traveled to Yunzhong and stayed at Nantang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled to Yunzhong and took up residence at Nantang Temple.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸，海雲禪師被召，過雲中，聞其博學多材藝，邀與俱行。

translations.literal: When the future Shizu was at his private residence, Chan Master Haiyun was summoned; passing through Yunzhong he heard that Bingzhong was learned and possessed many talents, and invited him to go along.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Shizu was still at his princely residence, Chan Master Haiyun was summoned to court; passing through Yunzhong he heard that Bingzhong was broadly learned and skilled in many arts, and invited him to travel together.

sentences.zh: 既入見，應對稱旨，屢承顧問。

translations.literal: Once he had been presented, his answers pleased the prince, and he was repeatedly consulted.
translations.idiomatic: After he was presented, his replies pleased the prince and he was consulted again and again.

sentences.zh: 秉忠於書無所不讀，尤邃於《易》及邵氏《經世書》，至於天文、地理、律曆、三式六壬遁甲之屬，無不精通。

translations.literal: Bingzhong read every kind of book without exception; he was especially profound in the Changes and in Shao Yong's Treatise on the Ages of the World; as for astronomy, geography, calendrics, the Three Styles, the Six Ren, the dunjia arts, and the like—there was none he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong read books of every kind; he was especially deep in the Book of Changes and Shao Yong's Treatise on the Ages of the World, and in astronomy, geography, calendrics, the Three Styles, Six Ren, dunjia, and the like there was nothing he did not master.

sentences.zh: 論天下事如指諸掌。

translations.literal: When he discussed affairs under Heaven it was as though he were pointing them out on the palm of his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of affairs under Heaven it was as if he were laying them out on his palm.

sentences.zh: 世祖大愛之，海雲南還，秉忠遂留籓邸。

translations.literal: The future Shizu cherished him greatly; when Haiyun returned south, Bingzhong remained at the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu came to love him dearly; when Haiyun returned south, Bingzhong stayed on at the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，奔父喪，賜金百兩為葬具，仍遣使送至邢州。

translations.literal: Several years later he rushed home upon his father's death; he was granted a hundred taels of gold for funeral expenses and envoys were still sent to escort him to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he hurried home for his father's funeral; he was granted a hundred taels of gold for burial expenses and an envoy was sent to accompany him to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 服除，復被召，奉旨還和林。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned again and, by imperial order, returned to Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was over he was summoned again and, by imperial order, returned to Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 上書數千百言，其略曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial of several thousand words; its gist ran as follows:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial of several thousand words; its gist was as follows:

sentences.zh: 典章、禮樂、法度、三綱五常之教​​，備於堯、舜，三王因之，五霸敗之。

translations.literal: The institutions, ritual and music, laws, and the teaching of the Three Bonds and Five Constants were fully established under Yao and Shun; the Three Kings inherited them, and the Five Hegemons corrupted them.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions, ritual and music, laws, and the teaching of the Three Bonds and Five Constants were fully realized under Yao and Shun; the Three Kings carried them on, and the Five Hegemons debased them.

sentences.zh: 漢興以來，至於五代，一千三百餘年，由此道者，漢文、景、光武，唐太宗、玄宗五君，而玄宗不無疵也。

translations.literal: From the rise of Han down to the Five Dynasties, in more than thirteen hundred years, those who followed this Way were the five rulers Wen and Jing of Han, Guangwu, Taizong of Tang, and Xuanzong—and even Xuanzong was not without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of Han down to the Five Dynasties, across more than thirteen hundred years, only five rulers truly followed this Way: Wen and Jing of Han, Guangwu, Taizong of Tang, and Xuanzong—and even Xuanzong was not without blemish.

sentences.zh: 然治亂之道，系乎天而由乎人。

translations.literal: Yet whether order or disorder prevails depends on Heaven and yet is realized through men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether the age is well governed or in turmoil rests with Heaven and is brought to pass through human effort.

sentences.zh: 天生成吉思皇帝，起一旅，降諸國，不數年而取天下。

translations.literal: Heaven produced the Genghis Emperor; he raised one column of troops, subdued all states, and within a few years took the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven produced Genghis Khan: he raised a single host, brought the states to submission, and within a few years seized the realm.

sentences.zh: 勤勞憂苦，遺大寶於子孫，庶傳萬祀，永保無疆之福。

translations.literal: Through toil and anxiety he bequeathed this great treasure to his descendants, hoping it might pass through ten thousand sacrifices and eternally preserve boundless felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Through labor and care he left this great inheritance to his descendants, hoping it might endure for ten thousand generations and forever secure boundless blessing.

sentences.zh: 愚聞之曰：「以馬上取天下，不可以馬上治。」

translations.literal: I have heard it said: "One may take the empire on horseback, but one cannot govern it on horseback."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said: "An empire won on horseback cannot be governed on horseback."

sentences.zh: 昔武王，兄也；

translations.literal: Of old King Wu was the elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity King Wu was the elder brother;

sentences.zh: 周公，弟也。

translations.literal: the Duke of Zhou was the younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Zhou was the younger.

sentences.zh: 周公思天下善事，夜以繼日，每得一事，坐以待旦，以匡周室，以保周天下八百餘年，周公之力也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou thought day and night of good deeds for the realm; whenever he grasped one matter he would sit awaiting dawn to carry it out, thereby supporting the Zhou house and preserving the Zhou realm for more than eight hundred years—the Duke of Zhou's power was this.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou pondered good for the realm day and night; whenever he grasped one matter he would sit awaiting dawn to act on it, thereby upholding the house of Zhou and preserving the Zhou realm for more than eight hundred years—such was the Duke of Zhou's power.

sentences.zh: 君上，兄也；

translations.literal: The prince is the elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is the elder brother;

sentences.zh: 大王，弟也。

translations.literal: the Great King is the younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: the Great King is the younger.

sentences.zh: 思周公之故事而行之，在乎今日。

translations.literal: To think upon the Duke of Zhou's example and act accordingly lies in the present day.
translations.idiomatic: To reflect on the Duke of Zhou's example and act upon it is a matter for this very day.

sentences.zh: 千載一時，不可失也。

translations.literal: Such an occasion comes once in a thousand years—it must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: An opportunity that comes once in a thousand years must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 君之所任，在內莫大乎相，相以領百官，化萬民；

translations.literal: Of what the prince must appoint within the realm, nothing is greater than a chief minister; the minister leads the hundred officials and transforms the myriad people;
translations.idiomatic: Among what Your Highness must appoint within the realm, nothing is greater than a chief minister, who leads the hundred officials and transforms the myriad people;

sentences.zh: 在外莫大乎將，將以統三軍，安四域。

translations.literal: outside, nothing is greater than a general; the general commands the Three Armies and secures the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: outside, nothing is greater than a general, who commands the Three Armies and secures the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 內外相濟，國之急務，必先之也。

translations.literal: Inner and outer supporting each other—this is the state's urgent matter and must be given priority.
translations.idiomatic: For inner and outer offices to support one another is the state's urgent business and must come first.

sentences.zh: 然天下之大，非一人之可及；

translations.literal: Yet the realm is vast and not within one man's reach;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the realm is vast and lies beyond what one man can encompass;

sentences.zh: 萬事之細，非一心之可察。

translations.literal: the myriad affairs are minute and not within one mind's scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: myriad affairs are minute and lie beyond what one mind can examine.

sentences.zh: 當擇開國功臣之子孫，分為京府州郡監守，督責舊官，以遵王法；

translations.literal: Those descendants of founding ministers should be chosen and assigned as supervisors and guards in the capital prefectures and commanderies to oversee the old officials so they observe the royal laws;
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the dynasty's founding ministers should be chosen and posted as supervisors in the capital, prefectures, and commanderies to oversee the old officials and enforce the royal laws;

sentences.zh: 仍差按察官守，治者升，否者黜。

translations.literal: surveying inspectors should also be dispatched; the competent should be promoted and the incompetent dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: surveillance commissioners should also be sent out to promote the able and dismiss the incompetent.

sentences.zh: 天下不勞力而定也。

translations.literal: Then the realm may be settled without exhausting the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm may be settled without exhausting the people.

sentences.zh: 天下戶過百萬，自忽都那演斷事之後，差徭甚大，加以軍馬調發，使臣煩擾，官吏乞取，民不能當，是以逃竄。

translations.literal: Households in the realm exceed a million; since the judicial office at Khodoein-Oron, corvée and levies have been very heavy; added to this are army and horse requisitions, the vexation of envoys, and officials' demands—the people cannot bear it, and for this reason they flee.
translations.idiomatic: Households in the realm number more than a million; since the judicial office at Khodoein-Oron, corvée and levies have grown very heavy, and to these are added military requisitions, the harassment of envoys, and officials' exactions—the people cannot endure it and therefore flee.

sentences.zh: 宜比舊減半，或三分去一，就見在之民以定差稅，招逃者復業，再行定奪。

translations.literal: Levies should be halved by comparison with the old rates, or reduced by one-third; fixed taxes should be assessed on those presently registered, the fugitives recalled to their occupations, and then a definitive reckoning made anew.
translations.idiomatic: Levies should be cut by half compared with former rates, or reduced by a third; taxes should be fixed on those presently registered, fugitives recalled to their fields, and then a definitive assessment made.

sentences.zh: 官無定次，清潔者無以遷，污濫者無以降。

translations.literal: Officials have no fixed grades; the honest have no way to advance, and the corrupt have no way to be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials have no fixed ranks: the upright have no path to promotion, and the corrupt no path to demotion.

sentences.zh: 可比附古例，定百官爵祿儀仗，使家足身貴。

translations.literal: Ancient precedents may be used as a model to fix the grades, salaries, and insignia of the hundred officials, so that their households are sufficient and their persons honored.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient precedents may be followed to fix the ranks, salaries, and regalia of the hundred officials, so that their households are secure and their persons honored.

sentences.zh: 有犯於民，設條定罪。

translations.literal: Those who harm the people should have statutes set and guilt determined.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wrong the people should have statutes drawn up and penalties defined.

sentences.zh: 威福者君之權，奉命者臣之職。

translations.literal: Majesty and favor belong to the prince's authority; receiving orders is the minister's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Majesty and favor belong to the ruler's prerogative; to receive and execute orders is the minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 今百官自行威福，進退生殺惟意之從，宜從禁治。

translations.literal: Now the hundred officials wield majesty and favor on their own; advancement, retreat, life, and death follow their whim—they should be forbidden and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials wield majesty and favor on their own; promotion, dismissal, life, and death follow their whim—this should be forbidden and corrected.

sentences.zh: 天下之民未聞教化，見在囚人宜從赦免，明施教令，使之知畏，則犯者自少也。

translations.literal: The people of the realm have not yet heard of moral instruction; those presently imprisoned should be pardoned, clear edicts issued to make them know awe, and then offenders will of themselves be few.
translations.idiomatic: The people have not yet received moral instruction; those now in prison should be pardoned and clear edicts issued to teach them reverence, and offenders will then grow few of themselves.

sentences.zh: 教令既設，則不宜繁，因大朝舊例，增益民間所宜設者十數條足矣。

translations.literal: Once edicts of instruction are established they should not be numerous; adding a dozen or so articles suitable for the people to the great court's old precedents is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Once instructional edicts are set they should not be numerous; adding a dozen or so articles suited to the people to the great court's old precedents is sufficient.

sentences.zh: 教令既施，罪不至死者皆提察然後決，犯死刑者覆奏然後聽斷，不致刑及無辜。

translations.literal: Once such edicts are enforced, in cases not deserving death all should be examined by the surveillance office before judgment; those guilty of capital crime should have their cases reported and reviewed before execution, so that punishment does not reach the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Once such edicts are in force, cases not warranting death should all be reviewed by the surveillance office before judgment; capital cases should be reported and re-examined before execution, so that the innocent are not punished.

sentences.zh: 天子以天下為家，兆民為子，國不足，取於民，民不足，取於國，相須如魚水。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven takes the realm as his home and the multitude as his children; when the state lacks, it is taken from the people; when the people lack, it is taken from the state—they need each other like fish and water.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven takes the realm as his home and the multitude as his children; when the state is short it draws on the people, and when the people are short they draw on the state—they depend on each other as fish on water.

sentences.zh: 有國家者，置府庫，設倉廩，亦為助民；

translations.literal: Those who possess a state establish treasuries and granaries also to assist the people;
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold a state establish treasuries and granaries also to aid the people;

sentences.zh: 民有身者，營產業，辟田野，亦為資國用也。

translations.literal: those who possess bodies cultivate estates and open fields also to supply the state's use.
translations.idiomatic: those who have bodies cultivate estates and open fields also to supply the state.

sentences.zh: 今宜打算官民所欠債負，若實為應當差發所借，宜依合罕皇帝聖旨，一本一利，官司歸還。

translations.literal: Now the debts owed by officials and people should be reckoned up; where loans were truly taken for obligatory levies and requisitions, in accordance with the sage edict of Emperor Khubilai principal and interest should be returned by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Debts owed by officials and people should now be reckoned; where loans were truly taken for obligatory levies, in accordance with the late emperor's edict principal and interest should be repaid by the government.

sentences.zh: 凡陪償無名，虛契所負，及還過元本者，並行赦免。

translations.literal: All debts with no name attached to compensation, false contracts, and those already repaid beyond the original principal should alike be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: All debts without proper title, false contracts, and sums already repaid beyond the original principal should alike be remitted.

sentences.zh: 納糧就遠倉，有一廢十者，宜從近倉以輸為便。

translations.literal: When grain tax is delivered to distant granaries and one measure in ten is lost, payment to nearer granaries should be permitted for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: When grain tax is delivered to distant granaries and one in ten is wasted, payment to nearer granaries should be allowed for convenience.

sentences.zh: 當驛路州城，飲食祗待偏重，宜計所費以準差發。

translations.literal: For prefectural cities on the courier routes, food and entertainment for guests are excessively burdensome; the cost should be calculated to set requisitions accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On courier routes, prefectural cities bear heavy costs for food and lodging; expenses should be calculated and requisitions set accordingly.

sentences.zh: 關市津梁正稅十五分取一，宜從舊制。

translations.literal: Regular tolls at passes and bridges should be one part in fifteen, following the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Regular tolls at passes and bridges should be one part in fifteen, following the old system.

sentences.zh: 禁橫取，減稅法，以利百姓。

translations.literal: Prohibit arbitrary exactions and reduce taxation methods to benefit the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Arbitrary exactions should be forbidden and tax burdens lightened to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 倉庫加耗甚重，宜令權量度均為一法，使錙銖圭撮尺寸皆平，以存信去詐。

translations.literal: Granary surcharges are very heavy; standardized weights and measures should be ordained as one law, so that scruple, grain, and cubic measures are all level, thereby preserving trust and removing fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Granary surcharges are very heavy; standardized weights and measures should be ordained as a single law so that every smallest unit is true, thereby preserving trust and rooting out fraud.

sentences.zh: 珍貝金銀之所出，淘沙煉石，實不易為，一旦以纏絲縷，飾皮革，塗木石，妝器仗，取一時之華麗，廢為塵而無濟，甚可惜也，宜從禁治。

translations.literal: Pearls, shells, gold, and silver come from refining sand and smelting stone and are truly not easily obtained; yet in an instant they are wound with silken thread, used to adorn leather, smeared on wood and stone, and made to ornament weapons and gear—seized for a moment's splendor, squandered to dust without benefit; this is deeply regrettable and should be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls, shells, gold, and silver are won only by washing sand and smelting ore and are not easily come by; yet in a moment they are wrapped in silk thread, used to adorn leather, smeared on wood and stone, and lavished on weapons and gear—spent for a moment's splendor and reduced to dust without profit. This is deeply wasteful and should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 除帝冑功臣大官以下章服有制外，無職之人不得僭越。

translations.literal: Apart from regulated robes for imperial kin, great ministers, and high officials, those without office must not transgress by imitation.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from regulated dress for imperial kin, great ministers, and high officials, those without office must not imitate them.

sentences.zh: 今地廣民微，賦斂繁重，民不聊生，何力耕耨以厚產業？

translations.literal: Now the land is wide and the people few; tax levies are heavy and the people have no leisure—how can they plough and cultivate to enrich their estates?
translations.idiomatic: The land is broad and the people few; levies are heavy and the people have no respite—how can they plough and sow to build up their estates?

sentences.zh: 宜差勸農官一員，率天下百姓務農桑，營產業，實國之大益。

translations.literal: An official to encourage agriculture should be dispatched to lead the people of the realm in sericulture and estate management—this would be a great benefit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: An official to encourage agriculture should be appointed to lead the people in sericulture and husbandry—this would be a great benefit to the state.

sentences.zh: 古者庠序學校未嘗廢，今郡縣雖有學，並非官置。

translations.literal: Of old, school and academy education was never abandoned; today although commanderies and counties have schools, they are not officially established.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity school and academy education was never abandoned; today although commanderies and counties have schools, they are not state-founded.

sentences.zh: 宜從舊制，修建三學，設教授，開選擇才，以經義為上，詞賦論策次之。

translations.literal: The old system should be followed to build the three schools, appoint professors, and open selection of talent, giving priority to the classics, with rhapsodies, discourses, and policy essays next.
translations.idiomatic: The old system should be restored: build the three schools, appoint professors, and open selection of talent, giving first place to the classics, with rhapsodies, discourses, and policy essays next.

sentences.zh: 兼科舉之設，已奉合罕皇帝聖旨，因而言之，易行也。

translations.literal: The establishment of the examination system has already been ordered by the sage edict of Emperor Khubilai; to speak of it again is easy to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: The civil service examinations have already been ordered by the late emperor's edict; to speak of them again is to urge what is already easy to enact.

sentences.zh: 開設學校，宜擇開國功臣子孫受教，選達才任用之。

translations.literal: In opening schools, descendants of founding ministers should be chosen to receive instruction, and outstanding talent selected and employed.
translations.idiomatic: In founding schools, descendants of founding ministers should be chosen to receive instruction, and outstanding talent selected for office.

sentences.zh: 天下莫大於朝省，親民莫近於縣宰。

translations.literal: Nothing under Heaven is greater than the court and ministries; nothing closer to the people than the district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing under Heaven is greater than the court and ministries; nothing closer to the people than the district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 雖朝省有法，縣宰宜擇，縣宰正，民自安矣。

translations.literal: Although the court has laws, the magistrate ought to be carefully chosen; when the magistrate is upright, the people will of themselves be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court has laws, the magistrate must be carefully chosen; when the magistrate is upright, the people will of themselves be at peace.

sentences.zh: 關西、河南地廣土沃，以軍馬之所出入，治而未豐。

translations.literal: The lands of Shaanxi and Henan are broad and fertile; yet because of the coming and going of army horses, though governed they are not yet prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Henan are broad and fertile, yet because armies and horses pass constantly through them, though governed they are not yet thriving.

sentences.zh: 宜設官招撫，不數年民歸土辟，以資軍馬之用，實國之大事。

translations.literal: Officials should be established to invite settlement; within a few years the people will return and the soil will be opened—this will supply military horses and is truly a great matter for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should be appointed to encourage settlement; within a few years the people will return and the land be opened—this will supply the armies and horses and is truly a great matter for the state.

sentences.zh: 移刺中丞拘榷鹽鐵諸產、商賈酒醋貨殖諸事，以定宣課，雖使從實恢辦，不足亦取於民，拖兌不辦，已不為輕。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Yisala monopolized salt, iron, and other products, and commercial levies on wine, vinegar, and trade profits to fix the official levy; even when required to raise funds in accord with facts, where insufficient it was again taken from the people, and failure to meet quotas was already no light burden.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yisala monopolized salt, iron, and other products and imposed commercial levies on wine, vinegar, and trade to fix official revenue; even when required to collect in accord with actual yields, shortfalls were again taken from the people, and failure to meet quotas was already no small hardship.

sentences.zh: 奧魯合蠻奏請於舊額加倍榷之，往往科取民間。

translations.literal: The Orokholman memorialized asking to double the monopoly over the old quota, and frequently imposed collection on the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Orokholman memorialized to double the monopoly over the old quota and often levied collections on the people.

sentences.zh: 科榷並行，民無所措手足。

translations.literal: Monopoly levies running together left the people with nowhere to put hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: With monopoly levies running together, the people had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 宜從舊例辦榷，更或減輕，罷繁碎，止科徵，無從獻利之徒削民害國。

translations.literal: The old monopoly quotas should be followed, or further lightened; cumbersome items abolished; only regular collection imposed—so that none who seek profit by harming the people may diminish the state.
translations.idiomatic: The old monopoly quotas should be followed, or further reduced; cumbersome items abolished and only regular levies imposed—so that none who seek profit by harming the people may injure the state.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨廢疾者，宜設孤老院，給衣糧以為養。

translations.literal: For widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, and the disabled, poorhouses for the aged should be established and clothing and grain supplied for their support.
translations.idiomatic: For widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, and the disabled, poorhouses for the aged should be established and clothing and grain provided for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 使臣到州郡，宜設館，不得於官衙民家安下。

translations.literal: When envoys reach prefectures and commanderies, lodgings should be provided; they must not be quartered in government offices or private homes.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys reach prefectures and commanderies, guest lodges should be provided; they must not be lodged in government offices or private homes.

sentences.zh: 孔子為百王師，立萬世法，今​​廟堂雖廢，存者尚多，宜令州郡祭祀，釋奠如舊儀。

translations.literal: Confucius was teacher to a hundred kings and established law for ten thousand generations; though temple halls today are ruined, many that remain should be ordered in prefectures and commanderies to offer sacrifice and libations according to the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius was teacher to a hundred kings and established law for ten thousand generations; though many temple halls are now ruined, those that remain should be ordered in prefectures and commanderies to offer sacrifice according to the old rites.

sentences.zh: 近代禮樂器具靡散，宜令刷會，徵太常舊人教引後學，使器備人存，漸以修之，實太平之基，王道之本。

translations.literal: In recent times ritual instruments and musical implements have been scattered and lost; an inventory should be ordered, retired officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices sought to instruct later students, so that implements are complete and men remain—gradually to be restored; this is truly the foundation of great peace and the root of the kingly Way.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times ritual instruments and musical implements have been scattered and lost; an inventory should be ordered and retired officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices sought to instruct later students, so that implements are complete and masters remain and may gradually be restored—this is truly the foundation of great peace and the root of the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 今天下廣遠，雖成吉思皇帝威福之致，亦天地神明陰所祐也。

translations.literal: Today the realm is vast; though this came through the majesty of Genghis Khan, it is also what Heaven and the spirits in the hidden realm bless.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is vast; though this came through Genghis Khan's majesty, it is also what Heaven and the spirits in the hidden realm bless.

sentences.zh: 宜訪名儒，循舊禮，尊祭上下神祇，和天地之氣，順時序之行，使神享民依，德極於幽明，天下賴一人之慶。

translations.literal: Renowned Confucians should be sought, old rites followed, and sacrifices to spirits above and below honored, harmonizing the qi of Heaven and Earth and following the seasons' sequence, so that spirits enjoy offerings and the people rely on them—virtue reaching to the hidden and manifest realms—and the realm relying on one man's blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned Confucians should be sought, old rites followed, and sacrifices to spirits above and below honored, harmonizing the qi of Heaven and Earth and following the seasons, so that spirits receive offerings and the people rely on them, virtue reaching to the hidden and manifest realms, and the realm secured by one man's blessings.

sentences.zh: :見行遼曆，日月交食頗差，聞司天臺改成新曆，未見施行。

translations.literal: The Liao calendar presently in use errs considerably in solar and lunar eclipses; it is heard that the Astrological Bureau has revised a new calendar which has not yet been implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao calendar now in use is considerably in error for solar and lunar eclipses; it is said the Astrological Bureau has compiled a new calendar that has not yet been promulgated.

sentences.zh: 宜因新君即位，頒曆改元。

translations.literal: On the new prince's accession the calendar should be promulgated and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the new ruler's accession the calendar should be issued and the era name changed.

sentences.zh: 令京府州郡置更漏，使民知時。

translations.literal: Let the capital prefectures and commanderies set clepsydra clocks so the people may know the time.
translations.idiomatic: The capital, prefectures, and commanderies should set water clocks so the people may know the hour.

sentences.zh: 國滅史存，古之常道，宜撰修《金史》，令一代君臣事業不墜於後世​​，甚有勵也。

translations.literal: When a state perishes its history is preserved—this is antiquity's constant rule; the History of Jin should be compiled so that one generation's ministers and achievements do not fall from later ages—this is greatly inspiriting.
translations.idiomatic: When a state perishes its history is preserved—this is antiquity's constant rule; the History of Jin should be compiled so that one generation's ministers and achievements are not lost to posterity—this would be greatly inspiriting.

sentences.zh: 國家廣大如天，萬中取一，以養天下名士宿儒之無營運產業者，使不致困窮。

translations.literal: The state is vast as Heaven; taking one in ten thousand to support eminent scholars and established Confucians without estates to manage, so they do not fall into want—
translations.idiomatic: The state is vast as Heaven; taking one man in ten thousand to support eminent scholars and established Confucians who possess no estates to manage, so they do not fall into want—

sentences.zh: 或有營運產業者，會前聖旨種養應輸差稅，其餘大小雜泛並行蠲免，使自給養，實國家養才勵人之大也。

translations.literal: or where they do manage estates, in accordance with prior sage edicts planting and raising should pay levies and taxes due; all other great and small miscellaneous impositions should be remitted together, so they may support themselves—this is truly the state's great work of nourishing talent and encouraging men.
translations.idiomatic: or where they do manage estates, in accordance with prior imperial edicts they should pay planting and raising taxes as due, while all other great and small miscellaneous levies should be remitted so they may support themselves—this is truly the state's great work of nourishing talent and encouraging men.

sentences.zh: 明君用人，如大匠用材，隨其鉅細長短，以施規矩繩墨。

translations.literal: An enlightened prince employs men as a great craftsman employs timber, following each piece's thickness, length, and shortness to apply compass, square, cord, and ink line.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler employs men as a master craftsman employs timber, fitting each piece's thickness, length, and shortness to compass, square, cord, and ink line.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「君子不可小知而可大受，小人不可大受而可小知。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "The noble man cannot be employed for petty knowledge yet can receive great responsibility; the petty man cannot receive great responsibility yet can be employed for petty knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "The noble man cannot be judged by petty tasks yet can bear great responsibility; the petty man cannot bear great responsibility yet can be judged by petty tasks."

sentences.zh: 蓋君子所存者大，不能盡小人之事，或有一短；

translations.literal: The noble man stores up what is great and cannot exhaust the petty man's affairs—or he may have one shortcoming;
translations.idiomatic: The noble man keeps what is great in view and cannot exhaust petty matters—or he may have one fault;

sentences.zh: 小人所拘者狹，不能同君子之量，或有一長。

translations.literal: the petty man is confined in what is narrow and cannot equal the noble man's measure—or he may have one strong point.
translations.idiomatic: the petty man is confined in what is narrow and cannot match the noble man's breadth—or he may have one strength.

sentences.zh: 盡其才而用之，成功之道也。

translations.literal: To employ each according to his talent—this is the way of success.
translations.idiomatic: To employ each according to his talent—this is the way to success.

sentences.zh: 君子不以言廢人，不以人廢言。

translations.literal: The noble man does not reject a man because of his words, nor reject words because of the man.
translations.idiomatic: The noble man does not reject a man because of his words, nor reject words because of the man.

sentences.zh: 大開言路，所以成天下、安兆民也。

translations.literal: To open wide the road of speech—this is how to accomplish the realm and settle the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: To open wide the road of counsel—this is how to perfect the realm and secure the multitude.

sentences.zh: 天地之大，日月之明，而或有所蔽。

translations.literal: As great as Heaven and Earth, as bright as sun and moon—yet they may sometimes be obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth are vast, sun and moon are bright—yet even they may sometimes be obscured.

sentences.zh: 且蔽天之明者，雲霧也；

translations.literal: Moreover, what obscures Heaven's brightness is cloud and mist;
translations.idiomatic: What obscures Heaven's brightness is cloud and mist;

sentences.zh: 蔽人之明者，私慾佞說也。

translations.literal: what obscures a man's clarity is private desire and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: what obscures a person's clarity is private desire and slanderous counsel.

sentences.zh: 常人有之，蔽一心也；

translations.literal: When ordinary men have these, they obscure one mind;
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary men have these, they obscure a single mind;

sentences.zh: 人君有之，蔽天下也。

translations.literal: when a ruler has them, he obscures the realm.
translations.idiomatic: when a ruler has them, he obscures the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 常選左右諫臣，使諷諭於未形，忖畫於至密也。

translations.literal: Remonstrating ministers at the ruler's side should be regularly chosen to admonish before faults take shape and to deliberate at the utmost depth.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating ministers at the ruler's side should be regularly chosen to counsel before faults take shape and to deliberate in the utmost secrecy.

sentences.zh: 君子之心，一於理義，懷於忠良；

translations.literal: The noble man's mind is single in principle and righteousness, filled with loyalty and goodness;
translations.idiomatic: The mind of the noble man rests wholly on principle and righteousness and is filled with loyalty and integrity;

sentences.zh: 小人之心，一於利欲，懷於讒佞。

translations.literal: the petty man's mind is single in profit and desire, filled with slander and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: the mind of the petty man rests wholly on profit and desire and is filled with slander and flattery.

sentences.zh: 君子得位，有容於小人；

translations.literal: When the noble man gains position he can tolerate the petty man;
translations.idiomatic: When the noble man gains position he can tolerate the petty man;

sentences.zh: 小人得勢，必排於君子。

translations.literal: when the petty man gains power he is sure to drive out the noble man.
translations.idiomatic: when the petty man gains power he is sure to drive out the noble man.

sentences.zh: 明君在上，不可不辨也。

translations.literal: When an enlightened ruler is above, this cannot but be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When an enlightened ruler sits above, this distinction cannot be neglected.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰「遠佞人」，又曰「惡利口之覆邦家者」，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Confucius said "Keep flatterers at a distance" and also said "I hate glib tongues that overturn states and clans"—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said "Keep flatterers at a distance" and also "I hate glib tongues that overturn states and families"—this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 今言利者眾，非圖以利國害民，實欲殘民而自利也。

translations.literal: Today those who speak of profit are many; they do not seek to benefit the state and harm the people, but in truth wish to injure the people for their own profit.
translations.idiomatic: Today those who speak of profit are many; they do not truly seek the state's good at the people's expense but wish to injure the people for their own gain.

sentences.zh: 宜將國中人民必用場冶，付各路課稅所，以定榷辦，其餘言利者並行罷去。

translations.literal: The indispensable workshops and smelters among the people of the realm should be entrusted to the tax offices of each circuit to fix monopoly quotas; all other profit-seekers should likewise be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Essential workshops and smelters among the people should be assigned to each circuit's tax office to fix monopoly quotas; all other profit-seekers should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 古者明王不寶遠物，所寶惟賢，如使賢者在位，能者在職，此皆一人之睿知，賢王之輔成也。

translations.literal: Of old enlightened kings did not treasure distant things; what they treasured was the worthy—if the worthy hold office and the capable hold posts, this is all one man's keen wisdom and the worthy king's assisting completion.
translations.idiomatic: Of old enlightened kings did not treasure exotic goods; what they treasured was talent—when the worthy hold office and the capable serve in posts, this rests on one man's keen wisdom and the worthy king's supporting hand.

sentences.zh: 古者治世均民產業，自廢井田為阡陌，後世因之不能復。

translations.literal: Of old in well-governed ages the people's estates were equalized; since the well-field system was abolished for crisscross paths, later ages inherited this and could not restore it.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity well-governed ages equalized the people's estates; since the well-field system was replaced by crisscross paths, later ages could not restore it.

sentences.zh: 今窮乏者益損，富盛者增加。

translations.literal: Today the destitute grow poorer while the wealthy increase.
translations.idiomatic: Today the destitute grow poorer while the rich grow richer.

sentences.zh: 宜禁行利之人勿恃官勢，居官在位者勿侵民利，商賈與民和好交易，不生擅奪欺罔之害，真國家之利也。

translations.literal: Those who pursue profit should be forbidden to rely on official power; those who hold office should not encroach on the people's profit; merchants and people should trade in good faith without the harm of arbitrary seizure and fraud—this is truly the state's profit.
translations.idiomatic: Profit-seekers should be forbidden to rely on official power; officeholders should not encroach on the people's livelihood; merchants and people should trade in good faith without arbitrary seizure or fraud—this is truly the state's gain.

sentences.zh: 笞箠之制，宜會古酌今，均為一法，使無敢過越。

translations.literal: The system of beating with bamboo and whip should gather ancient and modern precedents and be made one law, so that none dare transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for beating with rod and whip should reconcile ancient and modern practice into a single law so that none dare overstep.

sentences.zh: 禁私置牢獄，淫民無辜。

translations.literal: Private prisons should be forbidden, lest the people be wronged without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Private prisons should be forbidden so the innocent are not harmed.

sentences.zh: 鞭背之刑宜禁治，以彰愛生之德。

translations.literal: Whipping the back should be forbidden and corrected, to manifest the virtue of cherishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Back-whipping should be forbidden to manifest the virtue of cherishing life.

sentences.zh: 立朝省以統百官，分有司以御眾事，以至京府州郡親民之職無不備，紀綱正於上，法度行於下，是故天下不勞而治也。

translations.literal: Establish the court and ministries to govern the hundred officials, divide bureaus to manage the myriad affairs, down to the offices of capital, prefecture, and commandery that draw near the people—none should be lacking; when discipline is correct above and laws run below, therefore the realm is governed without toil.
translations.idiomatic: Establish the court and ministries to govern the hundred officials, divide bureaus to manage myriad affairs, down to the capital, prefectural, and commandery offices that serve the people—let none be lacking; when discipline is correct above and laws enforced below, the realm is governed without exhausting the people.

sentences.zh: 今新君即位之後，可立朝省，以為政本。

translations.literal: After the new ruler's accession, the court and ministries may be established as the foundation of government.
translations.idiomatic: After the new ruler's accession, the court and ministries should be established as the foundation of government.

sentences.zh: 其餘百官，不在員多，惟在得人焉耳。

translations.literal: As for the rest of the hundred officials, what matters is not their number but obtaining the right men.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest of the hundred officials, what matters is not their number but obtaining the right men.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The future Shizu praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 又言：「邢州舊萬餘戶，兵興以來不滿數百，凋壞日甚，得良牧守如真定張耕、洺水劉肅者治之，猶可完复。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Xingzhou formerly had more than ten thousand households; since the rise of arms it has not reached several hundred—the ruin grows daily worse; with good pastoral governors like Zhang Geng of Zhending and Liu Su of Luoshui it might still be restored."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Xingzhou once had more than ten thousand households; since warfare began it has fallen to fewer than several hundred, and ruin grows worse daily. With good governors like Zhang Geng of Zhending and Liu Su of Luoshui it might still be restored."

sentences.zh: 朝廷即以耕為邢州安撫使，肅為副使。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed Geng pacification commissioner of Xingzhou and Su as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed Geng pacification commissioner of Xingzhou and Su as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 由是流民復業，升邢為順德府。

translations.literal: Thereupon displaced people returned to their occupations and Xing was promoted to Shunde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon displaced people returned to their fields and Xing was promoted to Shunde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，從世祖徵大理。

translations.literal: In guichou he followed the future Shizu on the campaign against Dali.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou he followed the future Shizu on the campaign against Dali.

sentences.zh: 明年，徵雲南。

translations.literal: The next year he campaigned in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he campaigned in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 每贊以天地之好生，王者之神武不殺，故克城之日，不妄戮一人。

translations.literal: Each time he urged upon Heaven and Earth's love of life and the kingly spirit of martial prowess without slaughter; therefore on the day a city was taken not one person was rashly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he urged the ruler with Heaven and Earth's love of life and the kingly way of martial prowess without slaughter; therefore on the day a city was taken not one person was killed without cause.

sentences.zh: 己未，從伐宋，復以雲南所言力贊於上，所至全活不可勝計。

translations.literal: In jiwei he followed the attack on Song; again he strongly urged at court what he had said regarding Yunnan, and wherever he went the lives spared were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei he followed the attack on Song; again he strongly urged at court what he had said regarding Yunnan, and wherever he went the lives spared were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，問以治天下之大經、養民之良法，秉忠採祖宗舊典，參以古制之宜於今者，條列以聞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when the future Shizu took the throne, he asked about the great canon for governing the realm and good methods for nourishing the people; Bingzhong gathered the ancestral old statutes and, adding what was fitting in ancient systems for the present, listed them item by item and reported.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, when the future Shizu took the throne, he asked about the great principles for governing the realm and good methods for nourishing the people; Bingzhong gathered ancestral statutes and, adding what was fitting from ancient systems for the present, listed them and reported.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔建元紀歲，立中書省、宣撫司。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to establish the era name and year count, and to establish the Secretariat and pacification offices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict was issued to establish the era name and year count, and to establish the Secretariat and pacification offices.

sentences.zh: 朝廷舊臣、山林遺逸之士，咸見錄用，文物粲然一新。

translations.literal: Old ministers of the court and scholars hidden in mountains and forests were all employed, and cultural institutions shone with fresh splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Old ministers of the court and scholars hidden in mountains and forests were all employed, and cultural institutions shone anew.

sentences.zh: 秉忠雖居左右，而猶不改舊服，時人稱之為聰書記。

translations.literal: Although Bingzhong served at the emperor's side, he still did not change his old garb; people of the time called him Secretary Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Although Bingzhong served at the emperor's side, he still wore his old garb; people of the time called him Secretary Cong.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，翰林學士承旨王鶚奏言：「秉忠久侍藩邸，積有歲年，參帷幄之密謀，定社稷之大計，忠勤勞績，宜被褒崇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, Hanlin Academician Grand Preceptor Wang E memorialized: "Bingzhong has long served the princely residence, accumulating years of service; he participated in secret deliberations within the command tent and settled the great plans for the altars of state; his loyal diligence and achievements deserve reward and elevation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan, Hanlin Academician Grand Preceptor Wang E memorialized: "Bingzhong has long served the princely residence, accumulating years of service. He took part in secret deliberations within the command tent and settled the great plans for the altars of state. His loyal diligence and achievements deserve reward and elevation.

sentences.zh: 聖明御極，萬物惟新，而秉忠猶仍其野服散號，深所未安，宜正其衣冠，崇以顯秩。」

translations.literal: The sage emperor has ascended the throne and all things are made new, yet Bingzhong still wears rustic dress and bears unofficial titles—this is deeply unsettling; his robes and cap should be corrected and he should be elevated to a distinguished rank."
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor has ascended the throne and all things are made new, yet Bingzhong still wears rustic dress and bears unofficial titles. This is deeply unsettling; his robes and cap should be corrected and he should be elevated to a distinguished rank."

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，即日拜光祿大夫，位太保，參領中書省事。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and that same day invested him as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, appointed him Grand Preceptor, and made him participate in directing Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and that same day invested him as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, appointed him Grand Preceptor, and made him participate in directing Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔以翰林侍讀學士竇默之女妻之，賜第奉先坊，且以少府宮籍監戶給之。

translations.literal: An edict gave him the daughter of Hanlin Reader Dou Mo in marriage, granted a residence in Fengxian Ward, and assigned him households from the Directorate of Palace Provisions and household registers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gave him the daughter of Hanlin Reader Dou Mo in marriage, granted a residence in Fengxian Ward, and assigned him households from the Directorate of Palace Provisions and household registers.

sentences.zh: 秉忠既受命，以天下為己任，事無巨細，凡有關於國家大體者，知無不言，言無不聽，帝寵任愈隆。

translations.literal: Once Bingzhong accepted the appointment, he took the realm as his personal responsibility; whether matters were great or small, whenever they touched the fundamentals of state he spoke without holding back and nothing he said went unheard; the emperor's favor and trust grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bingzhong accepted the appointment, he took the realm as his personal responsibility. Whether matters were great or small, whenever they touched the fundamentals of state he spoke without holding back and nothing he said went unheard; the emperor's favor and trust grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 燕閑顧問，輒推薦人物可備器使者，凡所甄拔，後悉為名臣。

translations.literal: In informal audiences he would recommend men of capacity fit for service; of all those he selected, later every one became a noted minister.
translations.idiomatic: In informal audiences he would recommend men of capacity fit for service; of all those he selected, later every one became a noted minister.

sentences.zh: 初，帝命秉忠相地於桓州東灤水北，建城郭於龍岡，三年而畢，名曰開平。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had ordered Bingzhong to survey a site east of the Luan River at Huanzhou and build walls and moats at Longgang; in three years it was completed and named Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ordered Bingzhong to survey a site east of the Luan River at Huanzhou and build walls at Longgang; in three years it was completed and named Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 繼升為上都，而以燕為中都。

translations.literal: It was later promoted to Shangdu, and Yan was made Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: It was later promoted to the Upper Capital, and Yan was made the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，又命秉忠築中都城，始建宗廟宮室。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again ordered Bingzhong to build the Zhongdu city and first established the ancestral temple and palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again ordered Bingzhong to build the Central Capital and first established the ancestral temple and palace halls.

sentences.zh: 八年，奏建國號曰大元，而以中都為大都。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized to establish the state name as Great Yuan, and Zhongdu was made Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he memorialized to establish the state name as Great Yuan, and the Central Capital was made Dadu.

sentences.zh: 他如頒章服，舉朝儀，給俸祿，定官制，皆自秉忠發之，為一代成憲。

translations.literal: Other matters such as promulgating robes and caps, establishing court ritual, granting salaries, and fixing the official system all originated with Bingzhong and became institutions for a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Other matters such as promulgating robes and caps, establishing court ritual, granting salaries, and fixing the official system all originated with Bingzhong and became institutions for a generation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，扈從至上都，其地有南屏山，嘗築精舍居之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he accompanied the emperor to the Upper Capital; there was South Screen Mountain, where he had once built a refined hermitage and lived.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he accompanied the emperor to the Upper Capital; there was South Screen Mountain, where he had once built a hermitage and lived.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，秉忠無疾端坐而卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Bingzhong died without illness, seated upright, at fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Bingzhong died without illness, seated upright, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝聞驚悼，謂群臣曰：「秉忠事朕三十餘年，小心慎密，不避艱險，言無隱情。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was startled and grieved, and said to his ministers: "Bingzhong served me for more than thirty years, careful and discreet, not shunning hardship, speaking without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was startled and grieved and said to his ministers: "Bingzhong served me for more than thirty years, careful and discreet, not shunning hardship, speaking without concealment.

sentences.zh: 其陰陽術數之精，佔事知來，若合符契，惟朕知之，他人莫得聞也。」

translations.literal: His mastery of yin-yang arts and numerology, divining affairs and knowing what is to come, was as though matching tally seals—only I know this; others could not hear of it."
translations.idiomatic: His mastery of yin-yang arts and numerology, divining affairs and knowing what is to come, was as though matching tally seals—only I know this; others could not hear of it."

sentences.zh: 出內府錢具棺斂，遣禮部侍郎趙秉溫護其喪還葬大都。

translations.literal: He issued money from the inner treasury for the coffin and burial and sent Vice Minister of Rites Zhao Bingwen to escort the funeral back for burial in Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: He issued money from the inner treasury for the coffin and burial and sent Vice Minister of Rites Zhao Bingwen to escort the funeral back for burial in Dadu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，贈太傅，封趙國公，諡文貞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，贈太師，諡文正。

translations.literal: Under Chengzong he was further granted Grand Preceptor with posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzong he was further granted Grand Preceptor with posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，又進封常山王。

translations.literal: Under Renzong he was further advanced to Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Renzong he was further advanced to Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 秉忠自幼好學，至老不衰，雖位極人臣，而齋居蔬食，終日淡然，不異平昔。

translations.literal: Bingzhong loved learning from youth to old age without decline; though he reached the utmost of human rank, he lived on vegetables in fasting quarters, calm all day no different from before.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong loved learning from youth to old age without decline; though he reached the highest rank, he lived simply on vegetables, calm all day no different than before.

sentences.zh: 自號藏春散人。

translations.literal: He styled himself Hermit Who Hides Spring.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Hermit Who Hides Spring.

sentences.zh: 每以吟詠自適，其詩蕭散閒淡，類其為人。

translations.literal: He often took pleasure in chanting poetry; his poems were spare and tranquil, like the man himself.
translations.idiomatic: He often took pleasure in composing poetry; his poems were spare and tranquil, like the man himself.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He had collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟秉恕子蘭璋後。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took his younger brother Bingshu's son Lanzhang as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, he took his younger brother Bingshu's son Lanzhang as heir.

sentences.zh: 秉恕字長卿。

translations.literal: Bingshu, style name Zhangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Bingshu, styled Zhangqing.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，年弱冠，受《易》於劉肅，遂明理學。

translations.literal: He loved reading; in his early twenties he studied the Changes under Liu Su and thereby mastered Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading; in his early twenties he studied the Book of Changes under Liu Su and thereby mastered Neo-Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 兄秉忠，事世祖，以薦士自任，嫌於私親，獨不及秉恕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Bingzhong, serving the future Shizu, took recommending scholars as his charge and, scrupulous about private kin, alone did not recommend Bingshu.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Bingzhong, serving the future Shizu, took recommending scholars as his duty and, scrupulous about favoring kin, alone did not recommend Bingshu.

sentences.zh: 左右以聞，召見，遂同侍潛邸。

translations.literal: Those at the ruler's side reported this; he was summoned and then likewise attended the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Those at the ruler's side reported this; he was summoned and then likewise attended the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗賜秉忠白金千兩，辭曰：「臣山野鄙人，僥倖遭際，服器悉出尚方，金無所用。」

translations.literal: The future Shizu once granted Bingzhong a thousand taels of white gold; he declined saying: "I am a rustic of mountain and wilds who met with fortune by chance; my garments and vessels all come from the imperial workshops—gold is of no use to me."
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu once granted Bingzhong a thousand taels of white gold; he declined, saying: "I am a rustic of mountain and wild who met fortune by chance; my garments and vessels all come from the imperial workshops—gold is of no use to me."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「卿獨無親故遺之邪？」

translations.literal: The future Shizu said: "Have you no kin and friends to leave it to?"
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu said: "Have you no kin and friends to leave it to?"

sentences.zh: 辭不允，乃受而散之。

translations.literal: He could not decline further and accepted it and distributed it.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to decline further, he accepted it and distributed it.

sentences.zh: 以二百兩與秉恕，秉恕曰：「兄勤勞有年，宜蒙茲賞，秉恕無功，可冒恩乎？」

translations.literal: He gave two hundred taels to Bingshu; Bingshu said: "My elder brother has toiled for years and should receive this reward; Bingshu has no merit—how can I presume on favor?"
translations.idiomatic: He gave two hundred taels to Bingshu; Bingshu said: "My elder brother has toiled for years and should receive this reward; I have no merit—how can I presume on favor?"

sentences.zh: 終不受。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，擢禮部侍郎、邢州安撫副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and vice pacification commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and vice pacification commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，賜金符，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was granted a gold tally and transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was granted a gold tally and transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，升邢為順德府，賜金虎符，為順德安撫使。

translations.literal: In the third year Xing was promoted to Shunde Prefecture; he was granted a gold tiger tally and made pacification commissioner of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xing was promoted to Shunde Prefecture; he was granted a gold tiger tally and made pacification commissioner of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，轉官法行，改嘉議大夫，歷彰德、懷孟、淄萊、順天、太原五路總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, when the official system was reformed, he was changed to Grand Master for Glorious Discussion and served in succession as chief administrator of Zhangde, Huaimeng, Zilai, Shuntian, and Taiyuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan, when the official system was reformed, he was changed to Grand Master for Glorious Discussion and served in succession as chief administrator of Zhangde, Huaimeng, Zilai, Shuntian, and Taiyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 淄萊府有死囚六人，獄已具。

translations.literal: In Zilai Prefecture there were six condemned prisoners and the case was already concluded.
translations.idiomatic: In Zilai Prefecture there were six condemned prisoners and the case was already concluded.

sentences.zh: 秉恕疑之，詳讞得其實，六人賴以不死。

translations.literal: Bingshu doubted it; through detailed review he obtained the truth and the six men were spared death thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Bingshu doubted the case; through detailed review he obtained the truth and the six men were spared death.

sentences.zh: 他所至，皆有惠政。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he showed benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he showed benevolent government.

sentences.zh: 召除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出為淮西宣慰使，會省宣慰司，歷湖州、平陽兩路總管。

translations.literal: He went out as pacification commissioner of Huaixi; when the Huaixi pacification office was merged with the province, he served in succession as chief administrator of Huzhou and Pingyang circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as pacification commissioner of Huaixi; when the Huaixi pacification office was merged with the province, he served in succession as chief administrator of Huzhou and Pingyang circuits.

sentences.zh: 平陽歲荒，民艱食，輒開倉以賑之，全活者眾。

translations.literal: Pingyang suffered famine one year and the people had hard fare; he promptly opened granaries to relieve them and many were thereby preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingyang suffered famine and the people had hard fare, he promptly opened granaries to relieve them and many were preserved alive.

sentences.zh: 年六十，卒於官。

translations.literal: At sixty he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty he died in office.

sentences.zh: ○張文謙

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Wenqian
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Wenqian

sentences.zh: 張文謙，字仲謙，邢州沙河人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenqian, style name Zhongqian, was a man of Shahe in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenqian, styled Zhongqian, was a man of Shahe in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，善記誦，與太保劉秉忠同學。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and quick to memorize; he studied together with Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and quick to memorize; he studied together with Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong.

sentences.zh: 世祖居潛邸，受邢州分地，秉忠薦文謙可用。

translations.literal: When the future Shizu was at his private residence and received the Xingzhou allotment, Bingzhong recommended Wenqian as usable.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Shizu was at his princely residence and received the Xingzhou allotment, Bingzhong recommended Wenqian as capable.

sentences.zh: 歲丁未，召見，應對稱旨，命掌王府書記，日見信任。

translations.literal: In the dingwei year he was summoned and presented; his replies pleased the prince and he was ordered to manage the princely residence correspondence, gaining daily trust.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingwei year he was summoned and presented; his replies pleased the prince and he was ordered to manage the princely residence correspondence, gaining daily trust.

sentences.zh: 邢州當要衝，初分二千戶為勳臣食邑，歲遣人監領，皆不知撫治，徵求百出，民弗堪命，或訴於王府。

translations.literal: Xingzhou lay on a vital route; when the allotment was first made, two thousand households were set as fiefs for meritorious ministers; each year men were sent to supervise, none knowing how to comfort and govern—exactions issued on every side and the people could not bear their lot, some appealing to the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou lay on a vital route; when the allotment was first made, two thousand households were set as fiefs for meritorious ministers; each year men were sent to supervise who knew nothing of comfort and governance—exactions issued on every side and the people could not bear it, some appealing to the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 文謙與秉忠言於世祖曰：「今民生困弊，莫邢為甚。

translations.literal: Wenqian spoke with Bingzhong to the future Shizu saying: "Now the people's livelihood is exhausted and nowhere is it worse than Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian spoke with Bingzhong to the future Shizu, saying: "The people's livelihood is exhausted and nowhere is it worse than Xing.

sentences.zh: 盍擇人往治之，責其成效，使四方取法，則天下均受賜矣。」

translations.literal: Why not choose men to go govern it, hold them accountable for results, and let the four quarters take it as model—then the realm would equally receive blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Why not choose men to go govern it, hold them accountable for results, and let the four quarters take it as a model—then the whole realm would equally receive blessing."

sentences.zh: 於是乃選近侍脫兀脫、尚書劉肅、侍郎李簡往。

translations.literal: Thereupon those near at hand Tuotuotuo, Minister Liu Su, and Vice Minister Li Jian were chosen and sent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon those near at hand Tuotuotuo, Minister Liu Su, and Vice Minister Li Jian were chosen and sent.

sentences.zh: 三人至邢，協心為治，洗滌蠹敝，革去貪暴，流亡復歸，不期月，戶增十倍。

translations.literal: The three men reached Xing and worked together in governance, washing away corruption, removing greedy violence; displaced people returned, and within a month households increased tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: The three reached Xing and worked together in governance, washing away corruption and removing greedy violence; displaced people returned, and within a month households increased tenfold.

sentences.zh: 由是世祖益重儒士，任之以政，皆自文謙發之。

translations.literal: Thereby the future Shizu came to value Confucian scholars and employ them in government—all this began with Wenqian.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the future Shizu came to value Confucian scholars and employ them in government—all this began with Wenqian.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥，憲宗即位。

translations.literal: In the xinhai year Möngke ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinhai year Möngke ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 文謙與秉忠數以時務所當先者言於世祖，悉施行之。

translations.literal: Wenqian and Bingzhong often told the future Shizu what should be done first in affairs of the age, and all were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian and Bingzhong often told the future Shizu what should be done first in affairs of the age, and all were put into practice.

sentences.zh: 世祖征大理，國主高祥拒命，殺信使遁去。

translations.literal: When the future Shizu campaigned against Dali, the state lord Gao Xiang defied orders, killed the envoy, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Shizu campaigned against Dali, the state lord Gao Xiang defied orders, killed the envoy, and fled.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，將屠其城。

translations.literal: The future Shizu was enraged and was about to slaughter the city.
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu was enraged and was about to slaughter the city.

sentences.zh: 文謙與秉忠、姚樞諫曰：「殺使拒命者高祥爾，非民之罪，請宥之。」

translations.literal: Wenqian, Bingzhong, and Yao Shu remonstrated: "The one who killed the envoy and defied orders is Gao Xiang alone, not the crime of the people—please spare them."
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian, Bingzhong, and Yao Shu remonstrated: "The one who killed the envoy and defied orders is Gao Xiang alone, not the crime of the people—please spare them."

sentences.zh: 由是大理之民賴以全活。

translations.literal: Thereby the people of Dali were spared and preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the people of Dali were spared and preserved.

sentences.zh: 己未，世祖帥師伐宋，文謙與秉忠言：「王者之師，有征無戰，當一視同仁，不可嗜殺。」

translations.literal: In jiwei the future Shizu led armies against Song; Wenqian and Bingzhong said: "The army of a true king conquers without battle and should treat all alike under one benevolence—not indulge in slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei the future Shizu led armies against Song; Wenqian and Bingzhong said: "The army of a true king conquers without battle and should treat all alike under one benevolence—not indulge in slaughter."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「期與卿等守此言。」

translations.literal: The future Shizu said: "I expect to keep this word with you."
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu said: "I expect to keep this word with you."

sentences.zh: 既入宋境，分命諸將毋妄殺，毋焚人室廬，所獲生口悉縱之。

translations.literal: Once they entered Song territory, orders were issued to all generals not to kill without cause, not to burn people's dwellings, and to release all captives taken.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered Song territory, orders were issued to all generals not to kill without cause, not to burn people's dwellings, and to release all captives taken.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，立中書省，首命王文統為平章政事，文謙為左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when the future Shizu took the throne, the Secretariat was established; Wang Wentong was first appointed equal-rank administrator and Wenqian left vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, when the future Shizu took the throne, the Secretariat was established; Wang Wentong was first appointed equal-rank administrator and Wenqian left vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 建立綱紀，講明利病，以安國便民為務。

translations.literal: They established discipline and explained what was harmful and beneficial, taking securing the state and benefiting the people as their task.
translations.idiomatic: They established discipline and explained what was harmful and beneficial, taking securing the state and benefiting the people as their task.

sentences.zh: 詔令一出，天下有太平之望。

translations.literal: When edicts and orders issued forth, the realm had hope of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: When edicts and orders issued forth, the realm had hope of great peace.

sentences.zh: 而文統素忌克，謨謀之際，屢相可否，積不能平，文謙遽求出，詔以本官行大名等路宣撫司事。

translations.literal: Yet Wentong was by nature jealous and obstructive; in deliberations they often opposed each other and resentment accumulated; Wenqian hastily sought to leave and an edict sent him in his present office to conduct affairs of the Daming and other circuits pacification office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wentong was by nature jealous and obstructive; in deliberations they often opposed each other and resentment accumulated; Wenqian hastily sought to leave and an edict sent him in his present office to conduct affairs of the Daming and other circuits pacification office.

sentences.zh: 臨發，語文統曰：「民困日久，況當大旱，不量減稅賦，何以慰來甦之望？」

translations.literal: On departing he said to Wentong: "The people's distress has been long; moreover there is great drought—if we do not consider reducing taxes and levies, how can we comfort the hope of revival?"
translations.idiomatic: On departing he said to Wentong: "The people's distress has been long; moreover there is great drought—if we do not consider reducing taxes and levies, how can we comfort the hope of revival?"

sentences.zh: 文統曰：「上新即位，國家經費止仰稅賦，苟复減損，何以供給？」

translations.literal: Wentong said: "The new ruler has just taken the throne; state expenses rely solely on taxes and levies—if we again reduce them, how can we supply needs?"
translations.idiomatic: Wentong said: "The new ruler has just taken the throne; state expenses rely solely on taxes and levies—if we again reduce them, how can we meet needs?"

sentences.zh: 文謙曰：「百姓足，君孰與不足！

translations.literal: Wenqian said: "When the people are sufficient, who is the ruler not sufficient to?
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian said: "When the people are sufficient, is the ruler not also sufficient?

sentences.zh: 俟時和歲豐，取之未晚也。」

translations.literal: Wait until times are harmonious and harvests abundant—taking then is not yet late."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until times are harmonious and harvests abundant—collecting then is not yet late."

sentences.zh: 於是蠲常賦什之四，商酒稅什之二。

translations.literal: Thereupon regular levies were remitted by four-tenths and commercial wine taxes by two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon regular levies were remitted by four-tenths and commercial wine taxes by two-tenths.

sentences.zh: 二年春，來朝，复留居政府。

translations.literal: In the second spring he came to court and again remained in the central government.
translations.idiomatic: In the second spring he came to court and again remained in the central government.

sentences.zh: 始立左右部，講行庶務，鉅細畢舉，文謙之力為多。

translations.literal: The left and right departments were first established and myriad affairs were carried out in detail—all largely through Wenqian's effort.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right departments were first established and myriad affairs were carried out in detail—largely through Wenqian's effort.

sentences.zh: 三年，阿合馬領左右部，總司財用，欲專奏請，不關白中書，詔廷臣議之，文謙曰：「分制財用，古有是理，中書不預，無是理也。

translations.literal: In the third year Ahmad took charge of the left and right departments and overall managed finances, wishing to memorialize solely without reporting to the Secretariat; an edict ordered court ministers to deliberate and Wenqian said: "Dividing management of finances has ancient precedent; for the Secretariat not to participate—there is no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ahmad took charge of the left and right departments and overall managed finances, wishing to memorialize solely without reporting to the Secretariat; an edict ordered court ministers to deliberate and Wenqian said: "Dividing management of finances has ancient precedent; for the Secretariat not to participate—there is no such precedent.

sentences.zh: 若中書弗問，天子將親蒞之乎？」

translations.literal: If the Secretariat does not inquire, will the Son of Heaven personally attend to it?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Secretariat does not inquire, will the Son of Heaven personally attend to it?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「仲謙言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhongqian's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zhongqian's words are correct."

sentences.zh: 至元元年，詔文謙以中書左丞行省西夏中興等路。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan an edict ordered Wenqian as left vice administrator of the Secretariat to conduct provincial affairs in Western Xia Zhongxing and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan an edict ordered Wenqian as left vice administrator of the Secretariat to conduct provincial affairs in Western Xia Zhongxing and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 羌俗素鄙野，事無統紀，文謙得蜀士陷於俘虜者五六人，理而出之，使習吏事，旬月間簿書有品式，子弟亦知讀書，俗為一變。

translations.literal: Qiang custom was by nature crude; affairs had no unified discipline; Wenqian obtained five or six Shu scholars who had fallen into captivity, sorted out their cases and released them, and had them study clerkly affairs; within a month or so documents had proper form, sons and younger brothers also knew how to read books, and custom was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang custom was by nature crude and affairs had no unified discipline; Wenqian obtained five or six Shu scholars who had fallen captive, sorted out their cases and released them, and had them study clerkly affairs; within a month documents had proper form, sons and younger brothers also knew how to read, and custom was transformed.

sentences.zh: 浚唐來、漢延二渠，溉田十數万頃，人蒙其利。

translations.literal: He dredged the Tanglai and Hanyan canals and irrigated several hundred thousand qing of fields; the people received the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Tanglai and Hanyan canals and irrigated several hundred thousand qing of fields; the people received the benefit.

sentences.zh: 三年，還朝。

translations.literal: In the third year, he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 諸勢家言有戶數千，當役屬為私奴者，議久不決。

translations.literal: Powerful families claimed households numbering in the thousands that ought to serve as their private slaves; the debate went unresolved for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families claimed thousands of households that should serve as their private slaves, and the debate dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 文謙謂以乙未歲戶帳為斷，奴之未佔籍者，歸之勢家可也，其餘良民無為奴之理。

translations.literal: Wenqian said that the household registers of the yiwei year should be taken as the cutoff; slaves not yet entered in the registers could be returned to the powerful families, but ordinary citizens had no reason to be made slaves.
