translations.idiomatic: Wenqian argued that the household registers of the yiwei year should be the cutoff: unregistered slaves might be returned to the powerful families, but there was no grounds for turning ordinary citizens into slaves.

sentences.zh: 議遂定，守以為法。

translations.literal: The decision was settled and observed as law.
translations.idiomatic: The decision was settled and upheld as law.

sentences.zh: 五年，淄州妖人胡王惑眾，事覺，逮捕百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Hu Wang, a sorcerer in Zizhou, deluded the masses; when the affair was discovered, more than a hundred people were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a Zizhou sorcerer named Hu Wang misled the people; when the plot was exposed, more than a hundred were arrested.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童以文謙言奏曰：「愚民無知，為所誑誘，誅其首惡足矣。」

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Antong, citing Wenqian's advice, memorialized: "The foolish people are ignorant and were deceived and led astray; executing the chief offenders is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Antong, citing Wenqian, memorialized: "The common people are ignorant and were led astray; it is enough to punish the ringleaders."

sentences.zh: 詔即命文謙往決其獄，惟三人坐棄市，餘皆釋之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately ordered Wenqian to go decide the case; only three were sentenced to public execution, the rest were all released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered Wenqian to adjudicate the case; only three were executed in the marketplace, and all the rest were released.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜大司農卿，奏立諸道勸農司，巡行勸課，請開籍田，行祭先農先蠶等禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Director of the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture; he memorialized to establish agricultural encouragement offices in each circuit, to tour and urge cultivation, and requested opening ceremonial fields and performing rites honoring the first farmer and first silk cultivator, among others.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Director of the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture. He memorialized to establish circuit-level offices to encourage farming, to tour the realm urging cultivation, and to open ceremonial fields and perform rites to the First Farmer and First Silkworm.

sentences.zh: 復與竇默請立國子學。

translations.literal: Again, together with Dou Mo, he requested establishing the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Dou Mo in requesting the establishment of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 詔以許衡為國子祭酒，選貴冑子弟教育之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xu Heng as Chancellor of the Directorate and selected sons of noble families to educate them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xu Heng Chancellor of the Directorate and selected sons of noble families for their education.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬議拘民間鐵，官鑄農器，高其價以配民，創立行戶部於東平、大名以造鈔，及諸路轉運司，干政害民，文謙悉於帝前極論罷之。

translations.literal: At the time Ahmad proposed seizing iron from the people, having the government cast farm tools and selling them at high prices to distribute to the people; establishing travelling household bureaus at Dongping and Daming to make paper money, and various circuit transport commissions—all interfering in government and harming the people; Wenqian argued against all of these vigorously before the emperor until they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ahmad proposed confiscating private iron, casting farm tools at state forges, and selling them at inflated prices to the people; he also proposed establishing travelling household bureaus at Dongping and Daming to print paper money, along with circuit transport commissions—all of which meddled in government and harmed the people. Wenqian argued against each measure before the throne until they were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬慮憲台發其奸，乃奏罷諸道按察司以撼之，文謙奏復其舊。

translations.literal: Ahmad feared the Censorate would expose his crimes, so he memorialized to abolish the circuit inspection commissions to undermine Wenqian; Wenqian memorialized to restore them to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad, fearing the Censorate would uncover his crimes, memorialized to abolish the circuit inspection commissions in order to undermine Wenqian; Wenqian memorialized to have them restored.

sentences.zh: 然自知為奸臣所忌，力求去。

translations.literal: Yet knowing himself to be envied by wicked ministers, he strove to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: But knowing himself to be hated by corrupt officials, he pressed hard to leave office.

sentences.zh: 會世祖以《大明曆》歲久浸差，命許衡等造新歷，乃授文謙昭文館大學士，領太史院，以總其事。

translations.literal: Just then the future Shizu, because the Great Illuminations Calendar had grown inaccurate over the years, ordered Xu Heng and others to compile a new calendar; Wenqian was then appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for the Glorification of Literature and put in charge of the Astronomical Bureau to oversee the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Just then, because the Great Illuminations Calendar had drifted out of accuracy over the years, the future Shizu ordered Xu Heng and others to compile a new calendar. Wenqian was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for the Glorification of Literature and placed in charge of the Astronomical Bureau to direct the project.

sentences.zh: 十九年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾薨於位，年六十八。

translations.literal: A little over a year later, he died of illness in office, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died of illness in office, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 文謙蚤從劉秉忠，洞究術數；

translations.literal: Wenqian studied early under Liu Bingzhong and thoroughly investigated numerology and astrology;
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian had studied early under Liu Bingzhong and mastered the arts of calculation and divination;

sentences.zh: 晚交許衡，尤粹於義理之學。

translations.literal: in later years he befriended Xu Heng and became especially refined in the study of moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: in later years he came to know Xu Heng and grew especially accomplished in the study of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 為人剛明簡重，凡所陳於上前，莫非堯、舜仁義之道。

translations.literal: As a man he was firm, clear, simple, and dignified; whatever he presented before the emperor was none other than the way of humaneness and righteousness of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: In character he was upright, lucid, restrained, and grave; everything he presented before the throne was the path of humaneness and righteousness taught by Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 數忤權幸，而是非得喪，一不以經意。

translations.literal: He often offended those in power and favor, yet gain and loss, right and wrong—he did not care for any of them.
translations.idiomatic: He often crossed those in power and favor, yet he never gave a thought to gain or loss, right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 家惟藏書數万卷。

translations.literal: His household kept only books numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His household held nothing but books, numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 尤以引薦人材為己任，時論益以是多之。

translations.literal: He especially took recommending talent as his personal responsibility, and public opinion increasingly praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He made recommending talent a personal duty, and contemporary opinion increasingly praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 累贈推誠同德佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封魏國公，諡忠宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously ennobled cumulatively as Faithful-in-Sincerity, Equal-in-Virtue, Aid-to-the-Dynasty Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the State with the Three Honors of Opening an Office, Upper Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with posthumous title Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled cumulatively as Faithful-in-Sincerity, Equal-in-Virtue, Aid-to-the-Dynasty Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the State with the Three Honors of Opening an Office, and Upper Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous title Loyal and Expansive.

sentences.zh: 長子晏，仕至御史中丞，贈陝西行省平章政事，封魏國公，諡文靖。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yan rose to Vice Director of the Censorate; posthumously ennobled as Equal-Rank Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan rose to Vice Director of the Censorate; he was posthumously ennobled Equal-Rank Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, and given the posthumous title Cultured and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: ○郝經

translations.literal: ○ Hao Jing
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hao Jing

sentences.zh: 郝經，字伯常，其先潞州人，徙澤州之陵川，家世業儒。

translations.literal: Hao Jing, courtesy name Bochang; his ancestors were men of Luzhou; they moved to Lingchuan in Zezhou, and the family for generations pursued Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jing, styled Bochang, came from a family originally of Luzhou that had moved to Lingchuan in Zezhou; for generations they devoted themselves to Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 祖天挺，元裕嘗從之學。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tian Ting—Yuan Yu once studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian Ting was once studied under by Yuan Yu.

sentences.zh: 金末，父思溫辟地河南之魯山。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin, his father Siwen opened land in Lushan, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin dynasty his father Siwen settled in Lushan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 河南亂，居民匿窖中，亂兵以火熏灼之，民多死，經母許亦死。

translations.literal: When Henan fell into chaos, residents hid in cellars; marauding soldiers smoked them out with fire and many people died; Jing's mother Lady Xu also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan fell into chaos, the people hid in underground cellars; marauding troops smoked them out with fire, and many died, including Jing's mother, Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 經以蜜和寒菹汁，決母齒飲之，即蘇。

translations.literal: Jing mixed honey with pickled vegetable brine, pried open his mother's teeth and made her drink it; she immediately revived.
translations.idiomatic: Jing mixed honey with pickled vegetable brine, forced open his mother's clenched teeth, and made her drink it; she immediately revived.

sentences.zh: 時經九歲，人皆異之。

translations.literal: At the time Jing was nine years old; everyone considered it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was then nine years old, and everyone regarded it as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 金亡，徙順天。

translations.literal: When the Jin fell, they moved to Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Jin they moved to Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 家貧，晝則負薪米為養，暮則讀書。

translations.literal: The family was poor; by day he carried firewood and grain to support them, and in the evening he read books.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor: by day he carried firewood and grain to support them, and in the evening he studied.

sentences.zh: 居五年，為守帥張柔、賈輔所知，延為上客。

translations.literal: After five years, he was noticed by the defensive commanders Zhang Rou and Jia Fu, who invited him as a distinguished guest.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he came to the attention of the local commanders Zhang Rou and Jia Fu, who took him in as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 二家藏書皆萬卷，經博覽無不通。

translations.literal: Both households' libraries held ten thousand scrolls each; Jing read broadly and mastered them all.
translations.idiomatic: Each household possessed a library of ten thousand scrolls, and Jing read widely until nothing was beyond his reach.

sentences.zh: 往來燕、趙間，元裕每語之曰：「子貌類汝祖，才器非常，勉之。」

translations.literal: Traveling between Yan and Zhao, Yuan Yu often said to him: "Your appearance resembles your grandfather's; your talent and capacity are extraordinary—strive hard."
translations.idiomatic: As he traveled between Yan and Zhao, Yuan Yu often told him, "You look like your grandfather, and your talent is extraordinary. Apply yourself."

sentences.zh: 憲宗二年，世祖以皇弟開邸金蓮川，召經，諮以經國安民之道，條上數十事，大悅，遂留王府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Möngke, the future Shizu, as the emperor's younger brother, opened a residence at Jindianchuan; Jing was summoned and consulted on the way to order the state and pacify the people; he submitted several dozen items in list form; greatly pleased, the prince kept him at the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Möngke, the future Shizu, then serving as the emperor's younger brother, established his residence at Jindianchuan and summoned Jing to consult him on the governance of the state and the welfare of the people. Jing submitted several dozen proposals in detail. Greatly pleased, the prince retained him at his court.

sentences.zh: 是時，連兵於宋，憲宗入蜀，命世祖總統東師，經從至濮。

translations.literal: At this time, war continued with Song; Möngke entered Shu; the future Shizu was ordered to command the eastern armies; Jing followed to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time war with Song continued; Möngke entered Shu and ordered the future Shizu to command the eastern armies. Jing accompanied him as far as Pu.

sentences.zh: 會有得宋國奏議以獻，其言謹邊防，守衝要，凡七道，遂下諸將議。

translations.literal: It happened that someone obtained and presented Song memorials on policy; they spoke of carefully guarding the frontier and holding strategic points—seven routes in all; the matter was then sent down for the generals to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then obtained and presented Song policy memorials urging careful border defense and the holding of strategic passes, setting out seven routes in all; the document was sent down for the generals to discuss.

sentences.zh: 經曰：「古之一天下者，以德不以力。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Those who unified the realm in antiquity did so by virtue, not by force.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Those who unified the realm in antiquity did so through virtue, not through force.

sentences.zh: 彼今未有敗亡之釁，我乃空國而出，諸侯窺伺於內，小民凋弊於外。

translations.literal: They have no sign of defeat and ruin now, yet we empty the state to go forth; feudal lords watch and wait within, the common people wither in hardship without.
translations.idiomatic: Song shows no sign of imminent collapse, yet we would empty the state to march forth while lords at home watch for their chance and the common people suffer abroad.

sentences.zh: 經見其危，未見其利也。

translations.literal: I see the danger, not the profit.
translations.idiomatic: I see the danger in this, not the gain.

sentences.zh: 王不如修德布惠，敦族簡賢，綏懷遠人，控制諸道，結盟飭備，以待西師。

translations.literal: Your Highness would do better to cultivate virtue and distribute benevolence, treat kin generously and select the worthy, soothe and cherish distant peoples, control the various circuits, form alliances and prepare defenses, and wait for the western armies.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness would do better to cultivate virtue and extend benevolence, treat your kin generously and select the worthy, soothe distant peoples, secure the circuits, form alliances, and ready your defenses while awaiting the western armies.

sentences.zh: 上應天心，下係人望，順時而動，宋不足圖也。」

translations.literal: Responding to Heaven's intent above and binding people's hopes below, acting when the time is right—Song is not worth plotting against."
translations.idiomatic: Align with Heaven above and with the people's hopes below, and move when the time is right—then Song will not be worth contending for."

sentences.zh: 世祖以經儒生，愕然曰：「汝與張拔都議邪？」

translations.literal: The future Shizu, taking Jing for a mere Confucian scholar, said in astonishment: "Did you discuss this with Zhang Batu?"
translations.idiomatic: The future Shizu, surprised that a Confucian scholar should speak so, exclaimed, "Did you discuss this with Zhang Batu?"

sentences.zh: 經對曰：「經少館張柔家，嘗聞其論議。

translations.literal: Jing replied: "Jing lodged with Zhang Rou's household in his youth and once heard his deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered, "In my youth I lived in Zhang Rou's household and once heard his views.

sentences.zh: 此則經臆說耳，柔不知也。」

translations.literal: This is merely Jing's own speculation; Rou does not know of it."
translations.idiomatic: What I have just said is my own opinion; Rou knows nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 進七道議七千餘言。

translations.literal: He submitted a seven-thousand-plus-word memorial on the seven routes.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial of more than seven thousand characters on the seven routes.

sentences.zh: 乃以楊惟中為江淮荊湖南北等路宣撫使，經為副，將歸德軍，先至江上，宣布恩信，納降附。

translations.literal: Then Yang Weizhong was made Pacification Commissioner of the Jianghuai, Jinghu, Hunan, northern and southern, and other circuits, with Jing as deputy; leading the Guide army, they went first to the river and proclaimed benevolence and trust, accepting surrenders.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong was then appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Jianghuai, Jinghu, Hunan, and northern and southern circuits, with Jing as his deputy. Leading the Guide army, they went ahead to the river, proclaimed imperial benevolence and good faith, and received those who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 惟中欲私還汴，經曰：「我與公同受命南征，不聞受命還汴也。」

translations.literal: Weizhong wished to return privately to Bian; Jing said: "You and I received the same order to campaign south—I have not heard an order to return to Bian."
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong wished to go back privately to Bian, but Jing said, "You and I received the same commission to campaign south; I have heard no commission to return to Bian."

sentences.zh: 惟中怒，弗聽。

translations.literal: Weizhong grew angry and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong grew angry and refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 經率麾下揚旌而南，惟中懼謝，乃與經俱行。

translations.literal: Jing led his subordinates south with banners raised; Weizhong, afraid, apologized, and then went together with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led his troops south with banners flying. Weizhong, alarmed, apologized and then marched on with him.

sentences.zh: 經聞憲宗在蜀，師久無功，進《東師議》，其略曰：

translations.literal: Jing heard that Möngke was in Shu and the army had been long without success; he submitted the "Eastern Army Memorial," of which the gist was:
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Möngke was in Shu and that the campaign had dragged on without success, Jing submitted his "Eastern Army Memorial," the gist of which was as follows:

sentences.zh: 經聞圖天下之事於未然則易，救天下之事於已然則難。

translations.literal: Jing has heard that plotting matters of the realm before they arise is easy, while remedying matters of the realm after they have arisen is hard.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to plan for the realm before trouble arises is easy, but to rescue the realm once trouble has already arisen is hard.

sentences.zh: 已然之中復有未然者，使往者不失而來者得遂，是尤難也。

translations.literal: Within what has already arisen there are still matters not yet arisen; to make what is past not lost and what is to come able to succeed—this is especially hard.
translations.idiomatic: Even within what has already happened there remain things not yet happened; to keep the past from being lost and the future from being ruined is harder still.

sentences.zh: 國家以一旅之眾，奮起朔漠，斡鬥極以圖天下，馬首所向，無不摧破。

translations.literal: The state, with the host of a single brigade, rose up from the northern desert, wrestled with the pole to take the realm; wherever the horse's head pointed, nothing failed to be crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Our state, with the force of a single brigade, rose from the northern desert and wrestled with fate for the empire; wherever our horses turned, nothing stood unbroken.

sentences.zh: 滅金源，並西夏，蹂荊、襄，克成都，平大理，躪轢諸夷，奄徵四海，有天下十八，盡元魏、金源故地而加多，廓然莫與侔大也。

translations.literal: It destroyed the Jin, annexed Western Xia, trampled Jing and Xiang, took Chengdu, pacified Dali, crushed the various tribes, swept the four seas; held the realm for eighteen years, comprising all the former lands of Northern Wei and the Jin and more besides—vast, with none to equal its greatness.
translations.idiomatic: We destroyed the Jin, annexed Western Xia, overran Jing and Xiang, took Chengdu, pacified Dali, crushed the frontier peoples, and swept the four seas. For eighteen years we held the realm, encompassing all the old territories of Northern Wei and the Jin and more besides—vast beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 惟宋不下，未能混一，連兵構禍逾二十年。

translations.literal: Only Song would not submit; unification could not be achieved; connected warfare brought disaster for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Only Song would not submit, and unification remained incomplete; linked campaigns have brought disaster for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 何曩時掇取之易，而今日圖惟之難也？

translations.literal: Why was it easy to seize before, yet hard to plan for today?
translations.idiomatic: Why was it once so easy to take, and now so hard even to plan?

sentences.zh: 夫取天下，有可以力並，有可以術圖。

translations.literal: To take the realm, some may be absorbed by force, some may be plotted by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In taking the realm, some conquests may be won by force and others secured by strategy.

sentences.zh: 並之以力則不可久，久則頓弊而不振；

translations.literal: Absorbing by force cannot last long; prolonged, one becomes exhausted and feeble and cannot revive;
translations.idiomatic: Force cannot be sustained for long; drawn out, it grows spent and slack and cannot recover.

sentences.zh: 圖之以術則不可急，急則僥倖而難成。

translations.literal: Plotting by strategy cannot be rushed; rushed, one relies on luck and success is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Strategy cannot be hurried; hurried, it turns on chance and is hard to bring to completion.

sentences.zh: 故自漢、唐以來，樹立攻取，或五六年，未有逾十年者，是以其力不弊，而卒能保大定功。

translations.literal: Therefore from Han and Tang onward, campaigns of establishment and conquest lasted five or six years, never exceeding ten—thus force was not exhausted and in the end great achievements could be secured and settled.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Tang onward, founding conquests lasted five or six years and never more than ten, so that force was not exhausted and great success could at last be secured.

sentences.zh: 晉之取吳，隋之取陳，皆經營比佽十有餘年，是以其術得成，而卒能混一。

translations.literal: Jin's taking of Wu and Sui's taking of Chen both involved careful preparation for more than ten years—thus strategy was fulfilled and in the end unification was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's conquest of Wu and Sui's conquest of Chen both required more than ten years of careful preparation, so that strategy ripened and unification was finally achieved.

sentences.zh: 或久或近，要之成功各當其可，不妄為而已。

translations.literal: Whether long or short, the essential point is that success comes when each thing is timely—simply not acting rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the time required is long or short, success comes only when action is timely and nothing is done rashly.

sentences.zh: 國家建極開統垂五十年，而一之以兵，遺黎殘姓，遊氣驚魂，虔劉劘盪，殆欲殲盡。

translations.literal: The state established the apex and opened its succession for nearly fifty years, yet relied solely on arms; surviving remnants and broken clans, wandering spirits and frightened souls, trembled and shattered, nearly wanting extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Our state has upheld the throne and opened its succession for nearly fifty years, yet has relied on arms alone; the surviving people and broken clans, their spirits shaken and their souls in terror, have been battered and scattered almost to extinction.

sentences.zh: 自古用兵，未有如是之久且多也，其力安得不弊乎！

translations.literal: Since antiquity in the use of troops, never has it been so long and so much—how could force not be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Never in history have arms been employed so long and so relentlessly—how could our strength not be exhausted!

sentences.zh: 且括兵率賦，朝下令而夕出師，躬擐甲胄，跋履山川，闔國大舉，以之伐宋而圖混一。

translations.literal: Moreover troops are conscripted and levies collected; an order in the morning and the army marches by evening; the ruler personally dons armor, traverses mountains and rivers; the whole state mounts a great effort to attack Song and seek unification.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, troops are conscripted and taxes collected; an order given in the morning sends armies out by evening; the ruler himself dons armor and crosses mountains and rivers; the whole state is mobilized in a great campaign against Song in pursuit of unification.

sentences.zh: 以志則銳，以力則強，以土則大，而其術則未盡也。

translations.literal: In will it is sharp, in force it is strong, in territory it is vast—yet strategy is not fully applied.
translations.idiomatic: In resolve we are keen, in strength we are mighty, in territory we are vast—yet strategy has not been fully applied.

sentences.zh: 苟於諸國既平之後，息師撫民，致治成化，創法立制，敷布條綱，上下井井，不撓不紊，任老成為輔相，起英特為將帥，選賢能為任使，鳩智計為機衡，平賦以足用，屯農以足食，內治既舉，外禦亦備。

translations.literal: If after the various states were pacified one had rested the armies and soothed the people, brought order to completion and transformation, created laws and established institutions, spread regulations and rules, made superiors and inferiors orderly and without confusion or disruption, entrusted seasoned men as ministers, raised outstanding men as generals, selected the worthy and capable as envoys and administrators, gathered wisdom and schemes as the pivot of policy, balanced levies to meet expenses, established garrison farming to meet food needs—internal governance fully accomplished and external defense also prepared.
translations.idiomatic: If, once the other states had been pacified, we had rested the armies and soothed the people, brought government to completion and civilization to fruition, created laws and established institutions, spread regulations throughout the realm, made high and low orderly and undisturbed, entrusted seasoned men with ministerial office, raised outstanding men as generals, selected the worthy and capable for service, gathered wisdom into the pivot of statecraft, balanced taxes to meet expenses, and established garrison farming to meet food needs, then internal order would have been complete and external defense secure.

sentences.zh: 如其不服，姑以文誥，拒而不從，而後伺隙觀釁，以正天伐。

translations.literal: If they did not submit, first use written proclamations; if they refused and would not comply, then watch for gaps and signs of disorder and launch the righteous punitive campaign ordained by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If they still would not submit, we could first send written proclamations; if they refused, we could then watch for openings and signs of disorder and launch the righteous punitive campaign ordained by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自東海至於襄、鄧，重兵數道，聯幟接武，以為正兵。

translations.literal: From the Eastern Sea to Xiang and Deng, heavy forces in several columns, banners linked and ranks joined—this as the main army.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Sea to Xiang and Deng, heavy forces in several columns, banners linked and ranks continuous, would serve as the main army.

sentences.zh: 自漢中至於大理，輕兵捷出，批亢抵脅，以為奇兵。

translations.literal: From Hanzhong to Dali, light forces darting forth swiftly, striking the vital point and reaching the flank—this as the strategic army.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanzhong to Dali, light forces darting swiftly to strike the enemy's vital point and threaten his flank would serve as the strategic army.

sentences.zh: 帥臣得人，師出以律，高拱九重之內，而海外有截矣。

translations.literal: With the right commanders, the army sets out according to discipline; seated high within the palace depths, yet the realm beyond the seas is bounded.
translations.idiomatic: With the right commanders and armies that march by rule, the ruler could sit high within the palace while the realm beyond the seas was secured.

sentences.zh: 是而不為，乃於間歲遽為大舉，上下震動，兵連禍結，底安於危，是已然而莫可止者也。

translations.literal: This not being done, instead every few years a great campaign is hastily launched; superiors and inferiors are shaken; war links with disaster; one ends in danger from safety—this is what has already happened and cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of doing this, a great campaign is launched every few years; court and country are shaken, war breeds disaster, and safety ends in peril. This is what has already happened and can no longer be stopped.

sentences.zh: 東師未出，大王仁明，則猶有未然者，可不議乎！

translations.literal: Before the eastern army sets out, Your Highness is benevolent and discerning—there are still matters not yet arisen; should we not deliberate?
translations.idiomatic: Before the eastern army marches, while Your Highness is still benevolent and clear-sighted, there remain matters not yet lost—should we not discuss them?

sentences.zh: 國家用兵，一以國俗為製，而不師古。

translations.literal: The state uses troops entirely according to national custom, not taking antiquity as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Our state wages war entirely by its own customs, without taking antiquity as its guide.

sentences.zh: 不計師之眾寡，地之險易，敵之強弱，必合圍把槊，獵取之若禽獸然。

translations.literal: Without considering whether forces are many or few, terrain difficult or easy, enemy strong or weak, they must surround and close in with spears held, hunting prey as if birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Without regard for the size of the army, the difficulty of the terrain, or the strength of the enemy, we must always surround the foe, spears at the ready, and hunt him down like birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 聚如丘山，散如風雨，迅如雷電，捷如鷹鶻，鞭弭所屬，指期約日，萬里不忒，得兵家之詭道，而長於用奇。

translations.literal: Gathering like hills and mountains, dispersing like wind and rain, swift as thunder and lightning, nimble as hawks and falcons; wherever the whip guides them, they keep to appointed days across ten thousand li without error—attaining the strategist's way of deception and excelling at using surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering like mountains, dispersing like wind and rain, swift as thunder and lightning, sharp as hawks and falcons, they obey the whip and keep to the appointed day across ten thousand li without fail. This is the strategist's way of deception, and our strength lies in the use of surprise.

sentences.zh: 自澮河之戰，乘勝下燕、雲，遂遺兵而去，似無意於取者。

translations.literal: From the battle at the Fen River, riding victory to descend on Yan and Yun, then leaving troops behind and departing—as if without intent to take.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of the Fen River we rode victory down into Yan and Yun, then withdrew our troops and departed—as if we had no intention of taking the land at all.

sentences.zh: 既破回鶻，滅西夏，乃下兵關陝以敗金師，然後知所以深取之，是長於用奇也。

translations.literal: Having broken the Uighurs and destroyed Western Xia, then sending troops down through Guan and Shan to defeat Jin forces—only then knowing how to take deeply: this is excelling at surprise.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking the Uighurs and destroying Western Xia, we sent troops down through Guan and Shan to defeat the Jin—only then learning how to take territory in depth. That was our excellence in surprise.

sentences.zh: 既而為斡腹之舉，由金、房繞出潼關之背以攻汴；

translations.literal: Then came the flank-assault maneuver: through Jin and Fang, circling behind Tong Pass to attack Bian;
translations.idiomatic: Then came the flank assault, passing through Jin and Fang to circle behind Tong Pass and strike at Bian;

sentences.zh: 為搗虛之計，自西和徑入石泉、威、茂以取蜀；

translations.literal: the plan to strike the empty point: from Xihe straight into Shiquan, Wei, and Mao to take Shu;
translations.idiomatic: the plan to strike where the enemy was empty, entering directly from Xihe through Shiquan, Wei, and Mao to take Shu;

sentences.zh: 為示遠之謀，自臨洮、吐番穿徹西南以平大理。

translations.literal: the scheme to show distance: from Lintao and Tibet cutting through the southwest to pacify Dali.
translations.idiomatic: and the scheme to feign distance, cutting from Lintao and Tibet through the southwest to pacify Dali.

sentences.zh: 皆用奇也。

translations.literal: All used surprise.
translations.idiomatic: All of these relied on surprise.

sentences.zh: 夫攻其無備，出其不意，而後可以用奇。

translations.literal: To attack where there is no defense, emerge where not expected—only then can surprise be used.
translations.idiomatic: Only by attacking where the enemy is unprepared and appearing where he does not expect can surprise be used.

sentences.zh: 豈有連百萬之眾，首尾萬餘里，六飛雷動，乘輿親出，竭天下，倒四海，騰擲宇宙，軒豁天地，大極於遐徼之土，細窮於委巷之民，撞其鐘而掩其耳，囓其臍而蔽其目，如是用奇乎？

translations.literal: How can one link a million troops, ten thousand li from head to tail, six imperial carriages thundering, the emperor personally going forth, exhausting the realm, overturning the four seas, hurling the cosmos, throwing open heaven and earth, reaching to the farthest frontier, examining down to alley dwellers—striking the bell while covering one's ears, biting one's navel while blocking one's eyes—is this how to use surprise?
translations.idiomatic: How can one mass a million men in a line ten thousand li long, with the imperial carriages thundering forward and the ruler himself taking the field, exhausting the realm, overturning the four seas, shaking heaven and earth, reaching to the farthest frontier and probing into every alley—striking the bell while stopping one's ears, biting one's navel while covering one's eyes—and call that the use of surprise?

sentences.zh: 是執千金之璧而投瓦石也。

translations.literal: This is clutching a jade disc worth a thousand gold and throwing it at tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: That is like clutching a jade disc worth a thousand gold and hurling it against tiles and stones.

sentences.zh: 其初以奇勝也，關隴、江淮之北，平原曠野之多，而吾長於騎，故所向不能禦。

translations.literal: At first they won by surprise: north of Guan, Long, and the Huai and Yang rivers there is much plain and open country, and we excel at cavalry—thus wherever we went none could resist.
translations.idiomatic: At first we won through surprise because north of Guan, Long, and the Huai and Yang rivers lie broad plains and open country, and we excel at cavalry, so that wherever we turned none could withstand us.

sentences.zh: 兵鋒新銳，民物稠夥，擁而擠之，郡邑自潰，而吾長於攻，故所擊無不破。

translations.literal: The army's edge was fresh and sharp, people and goods densely packed—pressing and crowding them, districts and towns collapsed on their own; and we excel at assault—thus wherever we struck nothing failed to break.
translations.idiomatic: Our armies were fresh and sharp, the enemy's people and goods densely packed; pressed and crowded, districts and towns collapsed of themselves, and because we excel at assault, nothing we struck failed to break.

sentences.zh: 是以用其奇而驟勝。

translations.literal: Therefore using surprise they won suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, by using surprise, we won so swiftly.

sentences.zh: 今限以大山深谷，厄以重險薦阻，迂以危途繚徑，我之乘險以用奇則難，彼之因險以製奇則易。

translations.literal: Now constrained by great mountains and deep valleys, blocked by layered peril and repeated obstacles, twisted by dangerous paths and winding tracks—for us to exploit terrain for surprise is hard; for them to use terrain to devise surprise is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are hemmed in by great mountains and deep valleys, choked by layered passes and repeated obstacles, and twisted along dangerous paths and winding tracks. For us to use terrain for surprise is hard; for the enemy to use terrain against us is easy.

sentences.zh: 況於客主勢懸，蘊蓄情露，無虜掠以為資，無俘獲以備役，以有限之力，冒無限之險，雖有奇謀秘略，無所用之。

translations.literal: Moreover guest and host—the disparity of position; hidden intent is exposed; no plunder to serve as resources, no captives to supply labor; with limited force braving unlimited peril—even if there are secret stratagems and concealed plans, there is nowhere to apply them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as invaders we are at a disadvantage; our intentions are exposed; we have no plunder for supplies and no captives for labor; with limited strength we brave limitless danger. Even the cleverest stratagems have nowhere to be applied.

sentences.zh: 力無所用與無力同，勇無所施與不勇同，計不能行與無計同。

translations.literal: Force with nowhere to apply it is the same as no force; courage with nowhere to deploy it is the same as no courage; plans that cannot be executed are the same as no plans.
translations.idiomatic: Strength with nowhere to apply it is no strength at all; courage with nowhere to deploy it is no courage at all; plans that cannot be executed are no plans at all.

sentences.zh: 泰山壓卵之勢，河海濯爇之舉，擁遏頓滯，盤桓而不得進，所謂強弩之末不能射魯縞者也。

translations.literal: The momentum of Mount Tai crushing an egg, the effort of rivers and seas washing away embers—yet blocked and stalled, circling without advancing—what is called "the tip of a strong crossbow cannot pierce a Lu silk."
translations.idiomatic: We have the momentum of Mount Tai crushing an egg and the power of rivers and seas extinguishing a flame, yet we are blocked and stalled, circling without advancing—like the tip of a strong crossbow that cannot pierce a piece of Lu silk.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，則宜救已然之失，防未然之變而已。

translations.literal: For present planning, one should remedy errors already made and guard against changes not yet arisen—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The plan for the present should be to remedy what has already gone wrong and guard against what has not yet gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 西師既構，猝不可解，如兩虎相鬥，猝入於岩阻，見之者辟易不暇，又焉能以理相喻，使之逡巡自退？

translations.literal: The western army having already clashed, it cannot suddenly be resolved—like two tigers fighting who suddenly plunge into rocky defiles; those who see them shrink back without leisure—how can one reason with them and make them withdraw of their own accord?
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign has already begun and cannot suddenly be undone. It is like two tigers fighting who plunge together into a rocky ravine: those who see them shrink back in terror. How then can reason persuade them to withdraw of their own accord?

sentences.zh: 彼知其危，竭國以並命，我必其取，無由以自悔，兵連禍結，何時而已。

translations.literal: They know their peril and exhaust the state in a struggle for life; we insist on taking them—there is no way to repent; war links with disaster—when will it end?
translations.idiomatic: Song knows its peril and will exhaust the state in a fight to the death; we insist on taking it and cannot turn back. War breeds disaster—when will it end?

sentences.zh: 殿下宜遣人禀命於行在所，大軍壓境，遣使喻宋，示以大信，令降名進幣，割地納質。

translations.literal: Your Highness should send someone to report to the imperial headquarters where the emperor is; with the great army pressing the border, send envoys to persuade Song, show great good faith, and require them to submit their name, present tribute, cede territory, and send hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should send someone to report to the emperor's headquarters. With the main army pressing the border, send envoys to Song, offer great assurances of good faith, and require them to submit formally, present tribute, cede territory, and send hostages.

sentences.zh: 彼必受命，姑為之和，偃兵息民，以全吾力，而圖後舉，天地人神之福也。

translations.literal: They will surely accept the command; for the moment make peace with them, halt arms and rest the people, preserve our strength, and plan for a later undertaking—this is the blessing of Heaven, Earth, humankind, and the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Song will surely accept; for the moment make peace, halt the war, and rest the people so that we preserve our strength for a later campaign. That would be a blessing for Heaven, Earth, humankind, and the spirits alike.

sentences.zh: 禀命不從，殿下之義盡，而後進吾師，重慎詳審，不為躁輕飄忽，為前定之謀，而一之以正大，假西師以為奇而用吾正。

translations.literal: If reporting to headquarters and they do not comply, Your Highness's righteousness will have been fully displayed; only then advance our army—be heavily cautious and thorough, do not be rash, light, or flighty; make plans in advance and unify them with rectitude and grandeur; borrow the western army as surprise force and use our main force.
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse the orders you report upward, Your Highness will have done all that righteousness requires; only then should our army advance—slowly, carefully, and without rash haste. Lay plans in advance, keep them upright and grand in scope, use the western campaign as a strategic diversion, and commit our main force where it counts.

sentences.zh: 比師南轅，先示恩信，申其文移，喻以禍福，使知殿下仁而不殺，非好攻戰辟土地，不得已而用兵之意。

translations.literal: When the army turns south, first display kindness and good faith, deliver official communications, instruct them on fortune and disaster, so they know Your Highness is benevolent and does not kill, that you do not love warfare and seizing territory, but use arms only when unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: When the army turns south, show kindness and good faith first: send official communications and explain the consequences of submission and resistance, so they understand that Your Highness is merciful and does not delight in killing, that you do not love war or the seizure of land, and that you take up arms only when you must.

sentences.zh: 誠意昭著，恩信流行，然後閱實精勇，別為一軍，為帳下之卒，舉老成知兵者俾為將帥，更直宿衛，以備不虞。

translations.literal: Once sincerity is clear and kindness and trust prevail, then inspect troops and select the brave and seasoned, form a separate army as headquarters troops, appoint mature men who know war as commanders, rotate guard duty, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Once sincerity is plain and kindness and trust have taken hold, review the troops and pick out the brave and seasoned. Form a separate army as Your Highness's personal force, appoint mature, experienced commanders, rotate guard duty, and keep reserves ready against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 其餘師眾，各畀侯伯，使吾府大官元臣分師總統，為戰攻之卒。

translations.literal: The remaining army masses, assign each to the princes and nobles, have the great officials and senior ministers of our headquarters divide and command them as assault troops.
translations.idiomatic: Assign the rest of the army to the princes and nobles, and have the great officials and senior ministers of our headquarters divide command among them as the assault force.

sentences.zh: 其新入部曲，瞢不知兵，雖名為兵，其實役徒者，使沿邊進築，與敵郡邑犬牙相制，為屯戍之卒。

translations.literal: The newly recruited units who blindly know nothing of war—though called soldiers, in fact laborers—have them advance along the border building fortifications, interlocking with enemy prefectures and districts like dog's teeth, as garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The newly recruited units, ignorant of war though called soldiers and in truth little more than laborers, should be sent forward along the border to build fortifications, locking with enemy prefectures and districts like interlocking teeth, as garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 推擇單弱，究竟逃匿，編葺部伍，使聞望重臣為之撫育，總押近裡故屯，為鎮守之卒。

translations.literal: Select out the weak, track down those who have fled and hidden, reorganize the units, appoint eminent ministers to nurture them, overall command of nearby old garrisons, as defense garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Winnow out the weak, round up deserters and fugitives, reorganize the ranks, and put eminent ministers in charge of their care and training. Place them under overall command of nearby old garrisons as defensive troops.

sentences.zh: 使掣肘之計不行，妄意之徒屏息，內外備禦無有缺綻，則制節以進。

translations.literal: So that checkmate schemes cannot work, reckless plotters hold their breath, internal and external defenses without flaw—then advance with restraint and control.
translations.idiomatic: Only when schemes to check and constrain us can no longer succeed, when reckless schemers dare not stir, and when defenses within and without are sound should the advance proceed—measured, controlled, and in due order.

sentences.zh: 既入其境，敦陳固列，緩為之行。

translations.literal: Once entered their territory, array formations solid and dense, advance slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside their territory, keep formations solid and dense, and advance slowly.

sentences.zh: 彼善於守而吾不攻，彼恃城壁以不戰老吾，吾合長圍以不攻困彼，吾用吾之所長，彼不能用其長。

translations.literal: They excel at defense and we do not attack; they rely on walls and battlements to wear us down without fighting; we combine in a long siege not attacking to wear them down; we use our strengths, they cannot use theirs.
translations.idiomatic: They are skilled at defense, so we do not assault them. They rely on walls and battlements to wear us down without fighting; we encircle them in a long siege and wear them down without fighting. We use our strengths; they cannot use theirs.

sentences.zh: 選出入便利之地為久駐之基，示必取之勢。

translations.literal: Choose a location convenient for ingress and egress as base for long encampment, display the momentum of certain capture.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a position convenient for advance and withdrawal as a base for a long encampment, and show the momentum of an army that means to take what it besieges.

sentences.zh: 毋焚廬舍，毋傷人民，開其生路，以攜其心，亟肄以疲，多方以誤，以弊其力。

translations.literal: Do not burn dwellings, do not harm the people, open paths of survival to win their hearts, drill them relentlessly to wear them out, use many methods to confuse, to exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Do not burn dwellings or harm the people. Leave them a way to live and so win their hearts. Harass them constantly to wear them down, and use many stratagems to confuse and exhaust their strength.

sentences.zh: 兵勢既振，蘊蓄既見，則以輕兵掠兩淮，杜其樵採而遏其糧路，使血脈斷絕，各守孤城，示不足取。

translations.literal: Once military momentum is raised and reserves are apparent, then send light troops to raid the Two Huai, block their firewood and foraging and cut their grain routes, sever the lifelines, each holding isolated cities, showing them not worth taking.
translations.idiomatic: Once our military momentum is strong and our reserves are in place, send light troops to raid the Two Huai, cut off firewood and foraging, and block grain routes. Sever their lifelines so that each city stands alone and seems not worth the cost of taking.

sentences.zh: 即進大兵，直抵於江，沿江上下，列屯萬灶，號令明肅，部曲嚴整，首尾締構，各具舟楫，聲言徑渡。

translations.literal: Then advance the main army straight to the Yangtze, up and down the river line camps with ten thousand stoves, orders clear and strict, units disciplined, head and tail linked, each with boats, proclaim direct crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Then advance the main army straight to the Yangtze. Up and down the river, line the banks with camps and ten thousand cooking fires. Keep orders clear and discipline strict, link van and rear, equip every unit with boats, and proclaim an intention to cross directly.

sentences.zh: 彼必震疊，自起變故。

translations.literal: They will surely be greatly shaken and raise disturbances among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely be thrown into dismay and raise disturbances among themselves.

sentences.zh: 蓋彼之精銳盡在兩淮，江面闊越，恃其岩阻，兵皆柔脆，用兵以來未嘗一戰，焉能當我百戰之銳！

translations.literal: For their elite troops are all in the Two Huai; the river surface is broad; they rely on rocky barriers; their soldiers are all soft and brittle; since the war began they have never fought a single battle—how can they withstand our battle-hardened elite!
translations.idiomatic: Their elite troops are all in the Two Huai. The river is broad, they rely on rocky barriers, and their soldiers are soft and untested; since the war began they have never fought a real battle. How can such men stand against our battle-hardened veterans?

sentences.zh: 一處崩壞，則望風皆潰，肱髀不續，外內限絕，勇​​者不能用而怯者不能敵，背者不能返而面者不能禦，水陸相擠，必為我乘。

translations.literal: Once one place collapses, all will flee at the sight of the wind; arm and thigh disconnected; outside and inside cut off; the brave cannot be used and the timid cannot fight; those at the rear cannot return and those at the front cannot defend; land and water pressing together—they will surely be caught by us.
translations.idiomatic: Once one point gives way, the rest will flee at the mere rumor of defeat. Arm and thigh will be severed, outer defenses cut off from inner reserves. The brave will have no room to fight and the timid will not stand. Those in the rear cannot retreat and those in front cannot hold. Pressed on land and water alike, they will fall into our hands.

sentences.zh: 是兵家所謂避堅攻瑕，避實擊虛者也。

translations.literal: This is what military strategists call avoiding the strong and attacking the weak, avoiding the solid and striking the empty.
translations.idiomatic: This is what strategists call avoiding the strong and striking the weak, shunning the solid and hitting the empty.

sentences.zh: 如欲存養兵力，漸次以進，以圖萬全，則先荊後淮，先淮後江。

translations.literal: If one wishes to preserve and nurture military strength, advance step by step for complete security, then first Jing then Huai, first Huai then the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to preserve strength and advance step by step toward complete security, then take Jing first and Huai next, Huai first and the Yangtze next.

sentences.zh: 彼之素論，謂「有荊、襄則可以保淮甸，有淮甸則可以保江南」。

translations.literal: Their long-standing doctrine says, "With Jing and Xiang one can protect the Huai region; with the Huai region one can protect Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: Their long-standing doctrine holds that "with Jing and Xiang one can hold the Huai region, and with the Huai region one can hold Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 先是，我嘗有荊、襄，有淮甸，有上流，皆自失之。

translations.literal: Before this, we once had Jing and Xiang, had the Huai region, had the upper Yangtze—all lost through our own fault.
translations.idiomatic: We ourselves once held Jing and Xiang, the Huai region, and the upper Yangtze—and lost them all through our own errors.

sentences.zh: 今當從彼所保以為吾攻，命一軍出襄、鄧，直渡漢水，造舟為梁，水陸濟師。

translations.literal: Now we should take what they protect as our axis of attack—order one army out from Xiang and Deng, cross the Han River directly, build boats as bridges, transport troops by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should turn what they rely on to defend themselves into the axis of our attack: send one army out from Xiang and Deng, cross the Han River directly, build boats into bridges, and move troops by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 以輕兵掇襄陽，絕其糧路，重兵皆趨漢陽，出其不意，以伺江隙。

translations.literal: With light troops seize Xiangyang, cut their grain routes; heavy troops all rush to Hanyang, catch them unawares, to watch for openings on the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Send light troops to seize Xiangyang and cut their grain routes, while heavy forces rush on Hanyang by surprise and watch for an opening on the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 不然，則重兵臨襄陽，輕兵捷出，穿徹均、房，遠叩歸、峽，以應西師。

translations.literal: Otherwise, heavy troops press Xiangyang, light troops dash out, penetrate through Jun and Fang, strike far at Gui and Xia, to coordinate with the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, press Xiangyang with heavy troops while light forces dash through Jun and Fang, strike deep at Gui and Xia, and coordinate with the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 如交、廣、施、黔選鋒透出，夔門不守，大勢順流，即並兵大出，摧拉荊、郢，橫潰湘、潭，以成犄角。

translations.literal: If from Jiao, Guang, Shi, and Qian elite troops break through, if Kuimen is not held, the great momentum flowing downstream—then unite armies and advance in force, smash Jing and Ying, sweep across Xiang and Tan, to form pincers.
translations.idiomatic: If elite troops break out from Jiao, Guang, Shi, and Qian, if Kuimen is left undefended, and the main current sweeps downstream, then unite the armies and advance in force: smash Jing and Ying, sweep through Xiang and Tan, and form a pincer.

sentences.zh: 一軍出壽春，乘其銳氣，並取荊山。

translations.literal: One army out from Shouchun, riding their sharp momentum, also take Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Send one army out from Shouchun, ride its momentum, and take Jingshan as well.

sentences.zh: 駕淮為梁，以通南北。

translations.literal: Span the Huai as a bridge to connect north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Bridge the Huai to link north and south.

sentences.zh: 輕兵抄壽春，而重兵支佈於鍾離、合淝之間，掇拾湖濼，奪取關隘，據濡須，塞皖口，南入舒、和，西及於蘄、黃，徜徉恣肆，以覘江口。

translations.literal: Light troops raid Shouchun while heavy troops deploy between Zhongli and Hefei, gather lake marshes, seize passes, hold Ruxu, block Wankou, south into Shu and He, west to Qi and Huang, roam freely to reconnoiter the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Raid Shouchun with light troops while heavy forces spread between Zhongli and Hefei, secure the lake marshes, seize the passes, hold Ruxu, block Wankou, push south into Shu and He and west to Qi and Huang, and roam freely to reconnoiter the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 烏江、採石廣布戍邏，偵江渡之險易，測備御之疏密，徐為之謀，而後進師。

translations.literal: At Wujiang and Caishi widely post garrison patrols, scout the difficulty of river crossings, gauge the density of defenses, plan leisurely, then advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Wujiang and Caishi, post garrison patrols widely, scout the difficulty of crossings, measure the strength of defenses, plan at leisure, and only then advance the army.

sentences.zh: 所謂潰兩淮之腹心，抉長江之襟要也。

translations.literal: This is what is called rupturing the heart of the Two Huai and extracting the vital passes of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by rupturing the heart of the Two Huai and seizing the Yangtze's vital passes.

sentences.zh: 一軍出維揚，連楚蟠亙，蹈跨長淮，鄰我強對，通、泰、海門，揚子江面，密彼京畿，必皆備禦堅厚，若遽攻擊，則必老師費財。

translations.literal: One army out from Weiyang, connected to Chu sprawling across, treading the long Huai, neighboring our main adversary—Tong, Tai, Haimen, the Yangtze face of the Yangzi—close to their capital region, all surely heavily fortified; if attacked rashly, troops will be worn out and funds exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Send one army out from Yangzhou. Chu sprawls across this route; it crosses the long Huai and borders our chief enemy. Tong, Tai, Haimen, and the Yangzi stretch along the river face close to their capital region, and all are heavily fortified. A rash assault would only wear out the army and drain the treasury.

sentences.zh: 當以重兵臨維揚，合為長圍，示以必取。

translations.literal: Should press Weiyang with heavy troops, combine in long siege, show intent to take.
translations.idiomatic: Press Yangzhou with heavy troops, combine in a long encirclement, and show that it must be taken.

sentences.zh: 而以輕兵出通、泰，直塞海門、瓜步、金山、柴墟河口，遊騎上下，吞江吸海，並著威信，遲以月時，以觀其變。

translations.literal: While light troops out from Tong and Tai, directly block Haimen, Guabu, Jinshan, Chaiqu river mouth; roaming cavalry up and down, swallowing river and drawing in sea; all display authority and trust; delay for months to observe their changes.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile send light troops out from Tong and Tai to block Haimen, Guabu, Jinshan, and the Chaiqu river mouth. Let roaming cavalry move up and down the coast as if to swallow river and sea alike, show authority and restraint together, and wait months to watch how they respond.

sentences.zh: 是所謂圖緩持久之勢也。

translations.literal: This is what is called plotting for a slow, enduring momentum.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by building a slow, enduring strategic position.

sentences.zh: 三道並出，東西連衡，殿下或處一軍，為之節制，使我兵力常有餘裕，如是則未來之變或可弭，已然之失一日或可救也。

translations.literal: Three routes advancing together, east and west linked—Your Highness may station with one army to command and control, so our forces always have surplus; thus future troubles may perhaps be averted, and errors already made may one day be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: With three routes advancing together and east linked to west, Your Highness may take command of one army and coordinate the whole, keeping our forces always with reserve in hand. Then future disasters may yet be averted, and mistakes already made may one day be set right.

sentences.zh: 議者必曰：三道並進，則兵分勢弱，不若並力一向，則莫我當也。

translations.literal: Debators will surely say: three routes advancing together divides the army and weakens momentum—better to combine force in one direction, then none can withstand us.
translations.idiomatic: Critics will surely say that advancing on three routes divides the army and weakens its momentum, and that it would be better to combine all force in one direction so that none could stand against us.

sentences.zh: 會不知取國之術與爭地之術異：並力一向，爭地之術也；

translations.literal: They utterly fail to understand that the art of taking a state differs from the art of contesting territory: combining force in one direction is the art of contesting territory;
translations.idiomatic: They fail altogether to see that the art of conquering a state is not the art of seizing territory: to combine force in one direction is the art of seizing territory;

sentences.zh: 諸道並進，取國之術也。

translations.literal: advancing on all routes together is the art of taking a state.
translations.idiomatic: to advance on every route at once is the art of conquering a state.

sentences.zh: 昔之混一者，皆若是矣。

translations.literal: Those who unified the realm in the past all did thus.
translations.idiomatic: Every power that unified the realm in the past did the same.

sentences.zh: 晉取吳，則六道進；

translations.literal: Jin taking Wu—six routes advanced;
translations.idiomatic: When Jin took Wu, six routes advanced;

sentences.zh: 隋取陳，則九道進；

translations.literal: Sui taking Chen—nine routes advanced;
translations.idiomatic: when Sui took Chen, nine routes advanced;

sentences.zh: 宋之於南唐，則三面皆進。

translations.literal: Song against Southern Tang—all three sides advanced.
translations.idiomatic: and when Song moved against Southern Tang, it advanced on all three sides.

sentences.zh: 未聞以一旅之眾而能克國者，或者有之，僥倖之舉也。

translations.literal: Never heard of one brigade's force being able to conquer a state—if it ever happened, it was a lucky gamble.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of a single brigade conquering a whole state. If such a thing ever happened, it was luck, not strategy.

sentences.zh: 豈有堂堂大國，師徒百萬，而為僥倖之舉乎？

translations.literal: How can a great state in all dignity, with a million soldiers, make a lucky gamble?
translations.idiomatic: How can a great power in all its dignity, fielding a million men, stake everything on a lucky gamble?

sentences.zh: 況彼渡江立國，百有餘年，紀​​綱修明，風俗完厚，君臣輯睦，內無禍釁，東西南北，輪廣萬里，亦未可小。

translations.literal: Moreover they established their state south of the Yangtze for over a hundred years—institutions well ordered, customs complete and solid, ruler and ministers harmonious, no internal calamity within, east west north south spanning ten thousand li—not to be underestimated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Song has ruled south of the Yangtze for more than a century. Its institutions are well ordered, its customs sound, its ruler and ministers harmonious, and it has no internal strife. Its domain stretches ten thousand li in every direction. It is not to be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 自敗盟以來，無日不討軍實而申警之，徬徨百折，當我強對，未嘗大敗，不可謂弱。

translations.literal: Since breaking the alliance, not a day without mustering military strength and issuing warnings—wavering through a hundred turns, facing our main force, never suffered great defeat—cannot be called weak.
translations.idiomatic: Since the alliance was broken, not a day has passed without a muster of arms and a call to readiness. Though it has wavered and turned back upon itself a hundred times, it has faced our main force without suffering great defeat. It cannot be called weak.

sentences.zh: 豈可蔑視，謂秦無人，直欲一軍幸而取勝乎？

translations.literal: How can one despise them, say Qin has no men, and wish for one army to win by luck?
translations.idiomatic: How can we despise such a foe, pretend that "there is no one in Qin," and expect one army to win by sheer luck?

sentences.zh: 秦王問王翦以伐荊，翦曰：「非六十萬不可。」

translations.literal: The King of Qin asked Wang Jian about attacking Chu; Jian said: "Without six hundred thousand it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Qin asked Wang Jian about attacking Chu, Jian said, "It cannot be done with fewer than six hundred thousand men."

sentences.zh: 秦王曰：「將軍老矣。」

translations.literal: The King of Qin said: "General, you are old."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin said, "General, you are old."

sentences.zh: 命李信將二十萬往，不克，卒畀翦以兵六十萬而後舉楚。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Xin to lead two hundred thousand thither; they could not conquer; finally he gave Jian six hundred thousand troops and only then raised Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Xin with two hundred thousand men, but Li Xin failed. In the end he gave Jian six hundred thousand troops, and only then was Chu conquered.

sentences.zh: 蓋眾有所必用，事勢有不可懸料而幸取者。

translations.literal: For masses have uses that are indispensable; circumstances have outcomes that cannot be gambled on for lucky capture.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers have their necessary uses, and circumstances cannot be staked on a lucky stroke.

sentences.zh: 故王者之舉必萬全，其幸舉者，崛起無賴之人也。

translations.literal: Therefore the acts of true kings must be fully secure; those who gamble—they are upstart rabble.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the acts of a true king must be fully secure. Those who gamble on fortune are upstarts and adventurers.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 西師之出，已及瓜戍，而猶未即功。

translations.literal: The western army's departure has already reached the melon season, and still has not immediately achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign set out so long ago that the season has already turned to midsummer, and still it has not achieved its aim.

sentences.zh: 國家全盛之力，在於東左，若亦直前振迅，銳而圖功，一舉而下金陵、舉臨安則可也。

translations.literal: The state's full strength lies in the eastern flank; if it also presses straight forward swiftly, keen to seize victory, one stroke to take Jinling and Lin'an would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The state's full strength lies on the eastern front. If it presses straight forward with sharp resolve and takes Jinling and Lin'an in one stroke, that would be one thing.

sentences.zh: 如兵力耗弊，役成遷延，進退不可，反為敵人所乘，悔可及乎！

translations.literal: If military strength is exhausted, the campaign prolonged, advance and retreat impossible, and instead caught by the enemy—can regret help then!
translations.idiomatic: But if our strength is exhausted, the campaign drags on, advance and retreat alike become impossible, and the enemy turns our hesitation against us—then what good will regret do?

sentences.zh: 固宜重慎詳審，圖之以術。

translations.literal: One should indeed be heavily cautious and thorough, plan with strategy.
translations.idiomatic: This is exactly why one must be cautious, thorough, and deliberate, and plan by strategy rather than impulse.

sentences.zh: 若前所陳，以全吾力，是所謂坐勝也。

translations.literal: As stated before, to preserve our strength—this is what is called winning while seated.
translations.idiomatic: As I said before, to preserve our strength is what is called winning without fighting.

sentences.zh: 雖然，猶有可憂者。

translations.literal: Even so, there is still cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, there is still cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 國家掇取諸國，飄忽凌厲，本以力勝。

translations.literal: The state gathered and seized various kingdoms—swift and fierce—fundamentally winning by force.
translations.idiomatic: The state has gathered and seized kingdom after kingdom in swift, fierce campaigns, winning fundamentally by force.

sentences.zh: 今乃無故而為大舉，若又措置失宜，無以挫英雄之氣，服天下之心，則稔惡懷姦之流，得以窺其隙而投其間，國內空虛，易為搖盪。

translations.literal: Now for no reason undertaking a great campaign—if arrangements are again improper, unable to break the spirit of heroes and win the hearts of the realm, then those steeped in evil harboring treachery can spy the gaps and insert themselves; the interior hollow, easily shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Now, for no good reason, we launch a great campaign. If the arrangements are again mishandled and we fail to break the spirit of our heroes and win the hearts of the realm, then men long steeped in evil and treachery will spy our weaknesses and thrust themselves into the breach. The interior will be hollow and easily shaken.

sentences.zh: 臣愚所以諄諄於東師，反覆致論，謂不在於已然而在於未然者，此也。

translations.literal: This is why your servant's foolish self has been so earnest about the eastern army, arguing again and again that the concern lies not in what has already happened but in what has not yet happened.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have spoken so earnestly and at such length about the eastern campaign, insisting again and again that the danger lies not in what has already happened, but in what has not yet happened.

sentences.zh: 遂會兵渡江，圍鄂州，聞憲宗崩，召諸將屬議，經復進議曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered armies, crossed the Yangtze, and besieged Ezhou; hearing that Emperor Xianzong had died, Kublai summoned the generals for counsel; Jing again advanced his counsel, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the armies were united, the Yangtze was crossed, and Ezhou was besieged. When word came that Emperor Xianzong had died, the prince summoned his generals to counsel together, and Jing again offered his advice, saying:

sentences.zh: 《易》言：「知進退存亡而不失其正者，其惟聖人乎！」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Knowing advance and retreat, survival and destruction, and not losing the right way—is this not the sage alone?"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "He who knows when to advance and when to retreat, when to survive and when to perish, and does not lose the right course— is he not a sage?"

sentences.zh: 殿下聰明睿知，足以有臨；

translations.literal: Your Highness is intelligent and wise, sufficient to rule;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is intelligent and wise, fully equal to command;

sentences.zh: 發強剛毅，足以有斷。

translations.literal: resolute, strong, firm, and decisive, sufficient to decide.
translations.idiomatic: resolute, strong, and firm, fully equal to decide.

sentences.zh: 進退存亡之正，知之久矣。

translations.literal: The right way of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction—you have known it long.
translations.idiomatic: You have long known the right way of advance and retreat, survival and destruction.

sentences.zh: 向在沙陀，命經曰：「時未可也。」

translations.literal: Before at Shatuo, you charged Jing: "The time is not yet right."
translations.idiomatic: At Shatuo you once told me, "The time is not yet right."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「時之一字最當整理。」

translations.literal: You also said: "The word 'time' most deserves careful ordering."
translations.idiomatic: You also said, "Of all words, 'time' is the one that most deserves careful attention."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「可行之時，爾自知之。」

translations.literal: You also said: "When the time is right to act, you yourself will know."
translations.idiomatic: You also said, "When the time to act arrives, you yourself will know it."

sentences.zh: 大哉王言，「時乘六龍」之道，知之久矣。

translations.literal: How great the king's words! The way of "riding the six dragons in their time"—you have known it long.
translations.idiomatic: How great those words were! The way of "riding the six dragons at the proper time"—you have known it long.

sentences.zh: 自出師以來，進而不退，經有所未解者，故言於真定，於曹、濮，於唐、鄧。

translations.literal: Since the army marched out, advancing without retreating—what Jing has not understood—therefore spoke at Zhending, at Cao and Pu, at Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Since the army marched out and advanced without retreating—what I could not understand—I spoke at Zhending, at Cao and Pu, and at Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 亟言不已，未賜開允，乃今事急，故復進狂言。

translations.literal: Spoke urgently without cease, not granted approval; now that matters are urgent, therefore again advance these reckless words.
translations.idiomatic: I spoke urgently again and again, but received no approval. Now that matters are critical, I must again offer these rash words.

sentences.zh: 國家自平金以來，惟務進取，不遵養時晦，老師費財，卒無成功，三十年矣。

translations.literal: Since the state pacified Jin, it has pursued only advance, not heeding "nourish strength and bide one's time"—wearing out troops and wasting funds, ultimately no success—thirty years now.
translations.idiomatic: Since the state pacified the Jin, it has pursued advance alone and not heeded the lesson to nourish strength and bide one's time. For thirty years it has worn out its armies and wasted its treasury, yet achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 蒙哥罕立，政當安靜以圖寧謐，忽無故大舉，進而不退，畀王東師，則不當亦進也而遽進。

translations.literal: When Möngke Khan ascended, the government should have been quiet to seek tranquility—suddenly for no reason a great campaign, advancing without retreat; when the prince was given the eastern army, he should not have advanced yet but rushed to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke Khan came to the throne, the state should have rested and sought tranquility. Instead it suddenly launched a great campaign and advanced without retreat. When the prince was given the eastern army, he should not yet have marched—but he marched at once.

sentences.zh: 以為有命，不敢自逸，至於汝南，既聞凶訃，即當遣使，遍告諸帥，各以次退，修好於宋，歸定大事，不當復進也而遽進。

translations.literal: Thinking he had a commission, not daring to rest on his own, reaching Runan—once hearing the news of death, he should immediately have sent envoys to tell all commanders to withdraw in order, make peace with Song, return to settle the great matter—should not have advanced again but rushed to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had his orders and not daring to pause on his own account, he pressed on to Runan. Once he heard the news of the emperor's death, he should at once have sent envoys to every commander to withdraw in order, make peace with Song, and return to settle the succession. He should not have advanced further—but he advanced again at once.

sentences.zh: 以有師期，會於江濱，遣使喻宋，息兵安民，振旅而歸，不當復進也而又進。

translations.literal: Because there was a campaign deadline, meeting at the riverbank—should have sent envoys to persuade Song, halt arms and rest the people, withdraw the army and return—should not have advanced again but advanced once more.
translations.idiomatic: Because there was a campaign deadline, he met the armies at the riverbank. He should have sent envoys to Song to halt the war and rest the people, then withdrawn his forces and returned. He should not have advanced further—but he advanced again.

sentences.zh: 既不宜渡淮，又豈宜渡江？

translations.literal: Already unsuitable to cross the Huai—how can crossing the Yangtze be suitable?
translations.idiomatic: If it was already unwise to cross the Huai, how can it be wise to cross the Yangtze?

sentences.zh: 既不宜妄進，又豈宜攻城？

translations.literal: Already unsuitable to advance rashly—how can besieging a city be suitable?
translations.idiomatic: If it was already unwise to advance rashly, how can it be wise to besiege a city?

sentences.zh: 若以機不可失，敵不可縱，亦既渡江，不能中止，便當乘虛取鄂，分兵四出，直造臨安，疾雷不及掩耳，則宋亦可圖。

translations.literal: If one holds that opportunity cannot be lost and the enemy cannot be released—since already crossed the Yangtze and cannot stop—one should seize the moment take Ezhou, divide troops four ways, march straight to Lin'an, thunder before ears can be covered—then Song too could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: If one insists that the moment must not be lost and the enemy must not be allowed to recover—since the Yangtze has already been crossed and the advance cannot be halted—then one should seize the moment, take Ezhou, divide the army four ways, and strike straight for Lin'an like thunder before the ears can cover. Then Song might still be taken.

sentences.zh: 如其不可，知難而退，不失為金兀术也。

translations.literal: If that is not possible, knowing difficulty and withdrawing—would not fall short of Wanyan Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: If that is not possible, then knowing the difficulty and withdrawing would be no disgrace—no worse than Wanyan Zongbi.

sentences.zh: 師不當進而進，江不當渡而渡，城不當攻而攻，當速退而不退，當速進而不進，役成遷延，盤桓江渚，情見勢屈，舉天下兵力不能取一城，則我竭彼盈，又何俟乎？

translations.literal: Army should not advance but advanced, river should not be crossed but crossed, city should not be attacked but attacked; should quickly retreat but did not, should quickly advance but did not; campaign prolonged, lingering at the river isle, intentions revealed and momentum bent—all the realm's military power cannot take one city—we exhausted they full—what are we waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced when it should not have, the river was crossed when it should not have been, the city was attacked when it should not have been. We should have withdrawn quickly but did not; we should have pressed forward quickly but did not. The campaign drags on while we linger on the riverbank. Our intentions are exposed and our momentum broken. All the military power of the realm cannot take a single city. We are exhausted while the enemy is full. What, then, are we waiting for?

sentences.zh: 且諸軍疾疫已十四五，又延引月日，冬春之交，疫必大作，恐欲還不能。

translations.literal: Moreover plague among the armies already four or five parts in ten; delay month upon month—at the turn of winter and spring plague will surely rage—fear wishing to return but unable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, plague has already struck four or five men in ten throughout the armies. If we delay month after month until the turn of winter and spring, the pestilence will surely rage—and then we may wish to withdraw and be unable.

sentences.zh: 彼既上流無虞，呂文德已並兵拒守，知我國疵，鬥氣自倍。

translations.literal: They have no worry on the upper reaches; Lü Wende has already combined forces to resist; knowing our state's flaws, fighting spirit doubles of itself.
translations.idiomatic: They have no worry on the upper Yangtze. Lü Wende has already combined his forces to resist us. Knowing our weaknesses, their fighting spirit has doubled.

sentences.zh: 兩淮之兵盡集白鷺，江西之兵盡集隆興，嶺廣之兵盡集長沙，閩、越沿海巨舶大艦以次而至，伺隙而進。

translations.literal: Two Huai troops all gathered at Bailu, Jiangxi troops all at Longxing, Lingnan and Guang troops all at Changsha, Fujian and Zhejiang coastal great ships arriving in succession, watching for openings to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of the Two Huai are massed at Bailu, the Jiangxi forces at Longxing, the Lingnan and Guang troops at Changsha, and great ships from Fujian and Zhejiang are arriving along the coast one after another, waiting for an opening to strike.

sentences.zh: 如遏截於江、黃津渡，邀遮於大城關口，塞漢東之石門，限郢、復之湖濼，則我將安歸？

translations.literal: If blocked at the Jiang and Huang ferry crossings, intercepted at Dacheng Pass, the Shimen of eastern Han sealed, the lake marshes of Ying and Fu restricted—where shall our generals return?
translations.idiomatic: If we are blocked at the Jiang and Huang crossings, intercepted at Dacheng Pass, cut off at Shimen in eastern Han, and hemmed in by the lake marshes of Ying and Fu—where then can our army retreat?

sentences.zh: 無已則突入江、浙，搗其心腹。

translations.literal: If no alternative, burst into Jiang and Zhe, strike their heartland.
translations.idiomatic: If there is no other course, we would have to burst into Jiangsu and Zhejiang and strike their heartland.

sentences.zh: 聞臨安、海門已具龍舟，則已徒往；

translations.literal: Hearing Lin'an and Haimen already have dragon boats prepared—then going would be in vain;
translations.idiomatic: But if Lin'an and Haimen already have imperial barges ready, such a thrust would come to nothing;

sentences.zh: 還抵金山，並命求出，豈無韓世忠之儔？

translations.literal: returning to reach Jinshan, all ordered to sally forth—would there not be men like Han Shizhong?
translations.idiomatic: and on the return, when we reach Jinshan and the enemy is ordered out to meet us, will there not be commanders like Han Shizhong waiting?

sentences.zh: 且鄂與漢陽分據大別，中挾巨浸，號為活城，肉薄骨並而拔之，則彼委破壁孤城而去，溯流而上，則入洞庭，保荊、襄，順流而下，則精兵健櫓突過滸、黃，未易遏也，則亦徒費人命，我安所得哉！

translations.literal: Moreover Ezhou and Hanyang stand on either side of the Great Separation, with a vast lake between—called the Living City; if taken by pressing flesh against flesh and bone against bone, they would abandon the broken walls and leave as an isolated city; going upstream enters Dongting, securing Jing and Xiang; going downstream elite troops and strong oars burst past Hu and Huang—not easily stopped—then also merely wasting lives; what would we gain?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Ezhou and Hanyang stand on either side of Great Bi Mountain with a vast lake between them—a position called the Living City. Even if we took it only by pressing flesh to flesh and bone to bone, the defenders would abandon the broken walls and slip away. Upstream lies Dongting and the route to Jing and Xiang; downstream, elite troops and swift ships would burst past Hu and Huang and not easily be stopped. We would merely waste lives. What would we gain?

sentences.zh: 區區一城，勝之不武，不勝則大損威望，復何俟乎！

translations.literal: A mere single city—to conquer it is not martial glory; to fail greatly damages prestige—what are we waiting for!
translations.idiomatic: A single minor city: to take it would bring little glory, but to fail would greatly damage our prestige. What are we waiting for?

sentences.zh: 雖然，以王本心，不欲渡江，既渡江，不欲攻城，既攻城，不欲並命，不焚廬舍，不傷人民，不易其衣冠，不毀其墳墓，三百里外不使侵掠。

translations.literal: Even so, by the prince's true heart—he did not wish to cross the Yangtze; having crossed, did not wish to attack cities; having attacked, did not wish desperate struggle; does not burn dwellings, does not harm people, does not change their dress, does not destroy their tombs, beyond three hundred li does not permit raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, by the prince's own intent: he did not wish to cross the Yangtze; having crossed, he did not wish to attack cities; having attacked, he did not wish to stake everything on one throw. He would not burn dwellings, harm the people, change their dress, or destroy their tombs, and beyond three hundred li he would not permit raiding.

sentences.zh: 或勸徑趨臨安，曰其民人稠夥，若往，雖不殺戮，亦被踐蹂，吾所不忍。

translations.literal: Some urged hurrying straight to Lin'an; he said its people are densely gathered—if we go, even without slaughter they would be trampled—what I cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to strike straight for Lin'an. He said its people are densely packed; even without slaughter, they would be trampled underfoot—and that he could not bear.

sentences.zh: 若天與我，不必殺人；

translations.literal: If Heaven grants us victory, there is no need to kill people;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven grants us victory, there is no need to kill;

sentences.zh: 若天弗與，殺人何益，而竟不往。

translations.literal: if Heaven does not grant it, what good is killing—and in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: if Heaven does not grant it, what good would killing do? In the end he would not go.

sentences.zh: 諸將歸罪士人，謂不可用，以不殺人故不得城。

translations.literal: The generals blamed the scholar-officials, saying they were useless—because of not killing people they could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: The generals blamed the scholar-advisers, saying they were useless and that the city could not be taken because killing was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 曰彼守城者只一士人賈制置，汝十萬眾不能勝，殺人數月不能拔，汝輩之罪也，豈士人之罪乎！

translations.literal: He said: their defender is only one scholar-official, Commissioner Jia—your hundred thousand cannot defeat him; months of killing cannot capture it—the fault is yours, how is it the scholar-officials' fault!
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Their defender is only one scholar-official, Commissioner Jia. Your hundred thousand men cannot defeat him. Months of slaughter have not taken the city. The fault is yours—how is it the scholar-advisers' fault?"

sentences.zh: 益禁殺人。

translations.literal: He further forbade killing.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade killing all the more strictly.

sentences.zh: 巋然一仁，上通於天，久有歸志，不能遂行耳。
